title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Share a combinational non-restoring divider across DIV and REM
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median Fmax
5.442 MHz, and a 199.837 ns worst path spanning 156 cells through operand
forwarding, the ALU, and execute logic. There are no prior micro_opt
attempts or distilled lessons. The ALU contains separate signed and
unsigned division and remainder expressions; their deep combinational
arithmetic is the strongest suspected timing bottleneck. Since every
instruction shares this clock, a faster divider can improve CoreMark
throughput even when CoreMark executes few divisions.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with a single shared,
fully combinational, explicitly unrolled radix-2 non-restoring unsigned
quotient-and-remainder engine. Preserve the existing ALU interface,
zero-cycle combinational latency, pipeline registers, bus stalls, and
nret=1 retirement contract. This is an arithmetic implementation change,
with no multicycle execution, pipeline changes, or operation caching.

For DIV and REM, form 32-bit unsigned magnitudes using conditional
two's-complement negation; DIVU and REMU use the original operands.
Starting with a 33-bit partial remainder R=0, consume dividend bits
from bit 31 down to bit 0 in 32 elaboration-time-unrolled steps. If the
previous R is negative, the next R is (R << 1) + dividend_bit + divisor;
otherwise it is (R << 1) + dividend_bit - divisor. Each quotient bit is
the inverse sign of the updated R. Use explicit 33-bit unsigned bit
vectors and modulo-2^33 arithmetic; after each complete update R fits
the signed 33-bit range even though the intermediate shift can overflow.
Form the shifted dividend-insertion term as the wiring concatenation
{R[31:0], dividend_bit}, rather than an additional arithmetic operation.
Materialize the divisor and its 33-bit two's-complement negative once,
then select the addend with the preceding remainder sign so each digit
uses one carry-chain addition, without a separate magnitude comparator
or a restore mux following a subtraction. Correct the final unsigned
remainder by adding the divisor once if R is negative. Derive all four
operations from these shared quotient and remainder outputs, negating
the quotient when the signed operand signs differ and negating the
remainder when the signed dividend is negative.

Explicitly retain division-by-zero results (all-ones quotient, original
dividend remainder) and signed INT_MIN/-1 results (INT_MIN quotient,
zero remainder). Keep every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression exactly as
specified, excluding the real divider engine from ALTOPS builds, and
leave multiplication and base-integer operations alone.
Reducing duplicated arithmetic and eliminating compare/subtract/restore
logic at each division digit should lower ALU depth and routing pressure
without changing CoreMark cycles. The expected gain is a timing-driven
30 percent fitness improvement; Gowin mapping of the recurrence and the
final remainder/sign correction remain the main uncertainty.

Validate exact RV32M arithmetic using the existing ALU suite plus directed
and deterministic random division vectors, including divisors with bit
31 set, zero, one, powers of two and their neighbors, signed extrema,
quotient/remainder sign combinations, and long carry/borrow cases.
Require the unchanged formal and cosim gates and canonical CoreMark CRCs
under bus stalls. Compare Gowin median Fmax and worst paths, resource use,
and CoreMark bracketed cycles against the baseline; do not credit RVFI
logic pruning or placement noise as the improvement.

A width-faithful software model of this recurrence and signed wrapper
passed 87,380 exhaustive operand pairs at widths 1 through 8, including
divisor zero, and 59,208 directed/random signed and unsigned RV32 pairs.
This checks the proposed arithmetic algorithm, not the eventual RTL or
timing gain; no candidate FPGA timing measurement has been made.

title: Isolate division in a bounded multicycle execution unit
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz and its reported worst path traverses
forwarding and the execute ALU across 156 cells. The ALU currently infers
combinational signed and unsigned division and remainder networks, placing
deep arithmetic behind the ordinary EX operand muxes and ahead of the
registered result used for memory addresses and subsequent forwarding.
Removing these networks from single-cycle execution offers much more
timing headroom than a small improvement in instruction throughput. There
are no prior structural attempts or recorded lessons in this fixture.
Source inspection finds the visible divisions in CoreMark list sizing and
initialization, before the measured iteration loop; its timed list,
matrix, state, and CRC kernels therefore appear unlikely to pay a large
dynamic divide penalty. Confirm this with the unchanged bracketed cosim.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU with one shared, bounded multicycle
radix-2 restoring divider, leaving RV32I operations and multiplication on
their existing fast path. Register the fully forwarded operands and the
operation once when a valid divide instruction can start. Use registered
magnitude preparation, a 33-bit trial subtraction and one quotient-bit
update per iteration for exactly 32 iterations, and registered sign
correction. Use the trial subtraction's borrow to choose the restored
remainder instead of cascading a separate comparison and subtraction.
Both quotient and
remainder come from the same unsigned division state; select and sign them
according to the original instruction. Eliminate all synthesizable / and
% operators from the core ALU. Division by zero and signed overflow must
return the exact RV32M results, with a bounded completion handshake.

Keep the divide instruction in EX while it runs. Allow older EX/MEM and
MEM/WB instructions to drain, injecting fully zeroed bubbles into EX/MEM
when it is free, with valid, mem_read, mem_write, and reg_write all zero.
This prevents holding and replaying an older memory transaction.
Hold fetch and ID/EX until the divide result transfers exactly once into
EX/MEM. Capture forwarded operands at launch so retiring WB data cannot
disappear during the wait; retain the original instruction, PC, register
addresses, and captured operand values for RVFI. A completed result must
remain pending across dmem backpressure, with no relaunch or duplicate
retirement. Gate redirects and memory side effects by valid instruction
transfer, and preserve the existing load-use and WB forwarding rules.

Keep the core's nret=1 ports and decoder legality unchanged. Under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, implement the existing operation-specific XOR formulas
through the same request/completion interface with short bounded latency,
so the fixed formal depth continues to exercise operand routing and
retirement. Real simulation and FPGA synthesis must use the iterative
arithmetic. The hypothesis is that the Fmax increase from removing the
divider's deep combinational cone outweighs the extra divide cycles in
CoreMark; judge it using the unchanged median Gowin Fmax times bracketed
CoreMark iterations/cycle, including the existing random bus stalls.

title: Small tagged bimodal predictor removes correctly predicted redirect bubbles
motivation:
The baseline always fetches PC+4 and flushes the combinational fetch/decode
instruction whenever EX resolves a taken branch or jump. This costs one
bubble for each taken control transfer, including repeatedly taken loop
branches and calls. CoreMark executes these frequently. The measured worst
path runs through forwarding and the combinational M-extension ALU, so a
modest fetch predictor can improve iterations per cycle without extending
that dominant arithmetic path. Its timing and area costs must still be
measured rather than assuming that better prediction guarantees better fitness.
A retirement-trace model of the existing canonical CoreMark ELF counts
357,527 baseline redirect bubbles inside the markers and 73,619 successor
mispredictions with this 32-entry predictor. Against 4,491,485 baseline
cycles, that suggests a 6.75% gain if every avoided bubble saves a cycle,
or approximately 5.2% after estimating 22% overlap with instruction-bus
stalls, at unchanged Fmax. This is a sizing estimate, not an RTL or Gowin
measurement. A 64-entry direct-mapped table improves the same overlap
estimate only to 5.4%, so choose 32 entries to limit physical overhead.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry direct-mapped, fully tagged branch-target buffer with a
two-bit saturating direction counter per entry. Index by fetch PC[6:2],
store PC[31:7] as the tag and the full aligned target PC[31:2], and reset
valid bits. Read it combinationally from the registered fetch PC; a valid
tag hit with counter[1]=1 predicts the stored target, otherwise predict
PC+4. Use this lookup rather than instruction predecode or an IF target
adder. Train conditional branches on their resolved taken/not-taken
outcome, allocating at weakly taken (10) or weakly not taken (01), and
train aligned legal JAL/JALR targets as strongly taken (11). Train only
once when a valid EX instruction actually advances, never during reset,
bubbles, or dmem backpressure. Reject misaligned targets.

Carry the predicted successor PC through IF/ID and ID/EX with the
instruction. In EX compute the architectural successor using the existing
forwarded operands, branch/jump resolution, and misalignment handling.
Redirect and flush only when this actual successor differs from the
carried prediction. Check every valid instruction, including ordinary
instructions and traps, so a stale BTB hit or changed instruction cannot
silently send execution to the wrong path. Invalidate a matching entry
when its PC resolves as a non-control or otherwise ineligible instruction.
Correct predictions allow the currently fetched successor to enter ID/EX
without a bubble; all RVFI PC fields continue to report resolved values.

A prediction changes the PC only on the edge that accepts its instruction
into ID/EX; load-use, imem, and dmem stalls prevent ordinary PC advance.
Accept, hold, or clear prediction metadata together with its instruction,
following the existing stage enables and flush priorities. In particular,
imem stalls still insert an invalid ID/EX bubble while older EX work may
advance, and load-use still inserts the existing bubble. Gate EX recovery
with in.valid and !stall_ex_mem, preventing
repeated redirects while EX is held behind an older stalled memory op.
An eligible misprediction overrides imem/load-use holds, flushes the
younger instruction, and retries from the actual successor, even when
imemReady is low. Keep predictor lookup independent of redirect/flush
qualification to avoid a combinational control loop. Preserve the
existing nret=1 interface, decoding/traps, arithmetic, memory protocol,
retirement order, and all verification and benchmark contracts.

changes.description:

IF module, with EX training inputs, valid-bit reset, aligned targets,
replacement on tag misses, saturating branch updates, jump updates,
and stale-entry invalidation. Select the predicted successor on an
accepted fetch; recovery has priority over ordinary fetch holds.
Keep the predictor inline so existing explicit RTL source lists work.

Add a 32-bit predicted_next_pc field to if_id_t and id_ex_t only;

Compare it against in.predicted_next_pc for every valid advancing
instruction and make redirect_target the actual successor, including

once-per-advance predictor training information and suppress recovery
and training during dmem holds. Preserve resolved RVFI and link values.

Wire EX predictor training to IF and retain the existing hazard and
flush paths, now driven by prediction mismatches rather than every
taken transfer. Preserve all top-level ports and nret=1 retirement.

JALR targets, index collisions, and stale hits on replaced ordinary

branch held behind an older memory operation; check exactly-once
stores, retirement PCs/order, misaligned target traps, and flushed
wrong-path instructions. Check that a warmed taken loop avoids the
baseline redirect bubble using external cycle/retirement observations.

title: Remove redirect-driven payload masking with validity-only bubbles
motivation:
The registered divider champion scores 98.49 at a median 44.239 MHz,
with 4,491,817 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported 29.376 ns,
52-cell worst path now crosses ID, EX, IF, hazard logic, and ID again.
Fetch currently replaces the entire instruction with a NOP on redirect
or instruction-bus stall, so late recovery drives instruction bits,
register-file read addresses, decode, and load-use comparisons. ID also
clears its entire pipeline payload on a flush. These redundant bubble
encodings enlarge the recovery control cone even though validity already
suppresses execution. The prior micro_opt attempt retained a deep
combinational divider and gained only 17.57 percent over baseline; that
arithmetic bottleneck has already been removed in the current champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Represent fetch/decode bubbles solely through the existing valid bit,
removing late redirect and imem-stall signals from instruction payload
masking and from the synchronous clear of ID/EX data. This is one local
control-cone optimization, with the same pipeline boundaries, arithmetic
units, branch penalty, memory interface, and nret=1 retirement contract.

In if_stage, always expose raw imem_data as out.instr. Retain the current
out.valid qualification and PC update priorities: reset first, accepted
EX redirect next, then ordinary advance when not stalled. Decode,
immediate generation, and register-file read addresses must depend on
the raw fetched instruction rather than a redirect-selected NOP.

In id_stage, preserve the full reset initialization, but a nonreset flush
must clear only reg_q.valid. Give the non-valid payload fields a separate
update condition based only on !stall; they may capture raw data on a
flush when not stalled, or retain old data when stalled. Neither flush
nor input validity may select zero or disable capture for those fields.
Update valid with reset/flush priority, otherwise capture in.valid when
!stall, otherwise hold. This removes the late flush signal from the
wide operand, immediate, address, instruction, and control register muxes.

Since IF no longer supplies NOP register addresses on invalid fetches,
qualify the existing load-use comparison with imem_ready. Continue to
qualify the EX load through id_ex_w.valid at the core connection. Use
raw instruction rs fields without redirect-dependent masking or gating
by IF validity, which itself includes redirect. A valid EX load and a
valid EX redirect are mutually exclusive in this decoder; redirect
already overrides the PC hold and flushes ID/EX. Preserve dmem-stall and
execute-busy hold priority over a load-use bubble, and preserve the
existing MEM/WB data retention needed for forwarding during dmem holds.

Audit all consumers of possibly stale invalid ID/EX fields. Divider
request/consume, execute_busy, redirects, load-use detection, memory
side effects, and retirement must continue to require instruction
validity. EX must still emit its existing fully zeroed EX/MEM bubble for
invalid input, so invalid decoded mem_read, mem_write, or reg_write bits
never become live downstream. Keep decoder default-illegal behavior,
misalignment traps, RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic, and RVFI order unchanged.

The prediction is unchanged bracketed CoreMark cycles with roughly a
20 percent fitness gain from a shorter and less heavily loaded recovery
path. This is an estimate, not a measured result. Require existing unit,
formal, and stalled CoreMark cosim gates, exact canonical CRCs, and the
unchanged Gowin median timing evaluation. Check whether the reported
redirect-to-decode path disappears; a new arithmetic or memory critical
path may limit the gain. Acceptance still requires more than 4.6 percent
fitness improvement over 98.49, rather than an incidental placement gain.

An exhaustive software control model checked 1,310,720 legal combinations
of load destination and fetched source addresses, redirect/divide state,
both ready signals, and pending memory operations. The proposed
imem_ready-qualified raw-address load-use condition matched the current
NOP-masked condition throughout, using the decoder's mutual exclusion
of an EX load with an EX redirect or division. This supports the local
interlock transformation; it does not prove RTL correctness or timing.

title: Register branch recovery at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The champion's bounded divider raised median Gowin Fmax to 44.239 MHz
and fitness to 98.49. Its remaining reported worst path takes 29.376 ns
across 52 cells and traverses ID, EX, IF, hazard logic, and ID again.
The current EX redirect drives both the fetch instruction-to-NOP mux
and decode flush/load-use control combinationally, putting forwarded
branch resolution and frontend recovery in the same timing cone.
The prior structural attempt established that cutting a long execution
cone with registers can outweigh additional instruction latency. The
earlier predictor attempt reduced cycles by only 6.3% while retaining
the old divider bottleneck; it does not address this new feedback path.

earlier predictor attempt reduced cycles by only 6.3% while retaining
the old divider bottleneck; it does not address this new feedback path.

Move all architectural branch/jump recovery from combinational EX to
the registered EX/MEM boundary. This is one pipeline retiming change:
retain the champion's iterative divider, ordinary ALU datapath,
sequential fetch policy, memory interface, and nret=1 retirement width.
EX still computes forwarded comparisons, resolved targets, link values,
and target-alignment traps. Capture those results in EX/MEM as today,
but do not let the raw EX decision drive IF or ID control.

payload: valid, legal, and either a taken conditional branch or a jump.
Use its resolved pc_next as the redirect target, including JALR's
cleared low bit. Reuse the existing branch_taken and pc_next fields;
do not introduce a separate extra execution stage or delay non-control
instructions. Recovery changes fetch PC with priority over imem stalls
and ordinary holds and clears the younger ID/EX instruction. On that
same edge, explicitly squash the younger instruction currently in EX
by writing a fully zeroed EX/MEM bubble instead of its result. The
redirecting instruction proceeds normally through MEM/WB and retires
once with its original resolved PC, operands, link value, and trap data.

than the current one, without increasing steady-state ALU issue latency.

DIV/REM at the recovery edge must neither launch the divider nor consume
a completion nor keep execute_busy asserted; a younger store, load,
branch, illegal instruction, or register writer must never escape into
EX/MEM or retirement. Register the recovery decision only when EX really
advances, preserving an older stalled memory operation and the existing
retained WB forwarding data. A branch held in ID/EX behind dmem
backpressure must not redirect before it transfers into EX/MEM.

recovery must not wait for an unrelated low dmemReady. Clear or replace

once. Suppress recovery for bubbles, reset, decoder-illegal instructions,

title: Timing-conscious tagged prediction on the multicycle-divider champion
motivation:
The earlier predictor attempt, hyp-20261002-003-r1s2, reduced bracketed
CoreMark cycles from about 4.49 million to 4.21 million, a 6.3% reduction,
but retained the baseline combinational divider and therefore reached
only 5.577 MHz. This does not measure prediction on the current champion:
hyp-20261002-002-r1s1 already isolates division and reaches 44.239 MHz,
with 4,491,817 measured cycles and fitness 98.49. Reusing the demonstrated
cycle-saving opportunity now has a credible route above the 4.6%
acceptance margin. Timing deserves special care: the champion's reported
worst path traverses decode, execute, fetch, hazard, and decode again.
A predictor must avoid extending branch resolution with a serial
resolved-successor mux and wide equality comparator, or feeding recovery
through fetch-instruction substitution and register-file addresses.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one small, direct-mapped tagged bimodal branch-target predictor to
the existing fetch stage, on top of the current registered DIV/REM
implementation. Use 32 entries indexed by fetch PC[6:2], with a valid
bit, full PC[31:7] tag, aligned target PC[31:2], and a two-bit saturating
direction counter. A valid tag hit with counter[1] set selects the
stored target; otherwise select PC+4. Reset valid bits. Allocate legal,
aligned conditional branches at weakly taken or weakly not taken from
their actual outcome; update counters saturatingly on matching entries.
Learn JAL/JALR targets as strongly taken. Do not add global history, a
return stack, a cache, or changes to arithmetic execution.

Make recovery depend on prediction correctness, not simply on a taken
transfer. Carry prediction-selected and predicted-target metadata with
each accepted instruction. In decode, compute and register the direct
branch/JAL target and whether it equals the predicted target. This
comparison runs before EX and is independent of forwarded operands.
For an aligned legal conditional branch, EX recovery is direction
disagreement OR an actually taken branch with a target mismatch. JAL
uses the registered target-match result. JALR still resolves from the
actual forwarded rs1 plus immediate, clears bit 0, and checks its full
predicted target. For ordinary instructions, illegal instructions,
and a misaligned taken transfer, a selected nonsequential prediction
must recover to the existing architectural fall-through PC. This checks
stale predictions as well as control transfers. Preserve the existing
misalignment trap and suppression of jump link writes. Correctly
predicted transfers accept their fetched successor without a bubble;
recovery flushes the younger instruction and uses the resolved target
or fall-through. RVFI reports actual successors, never predictions.

Keep fetch instruction bits and predictor lookup independent of EX
recovery and flush qualification. Remove recovery-dependent NOP
substitution from the combinational fetch instruction/address path:
expose raw imemData, qualify fetch validity with imemReady and recovery,
and qualify load-use detection with fetch validity. Existing ID/EX
flush still clears its payload. Invalid fetch bits must not produce
hazards or architectural effects. This avoids the existing branch
resolution -> fetch NOP mux -> source-register addresses -> hazard/ID
control chain and prevents a predictor/recovery combinational loop.

Advance prediction, PC, and instruction metadata together only when
the instruction is accepted into ID/EX. All load-use, instruction-bus,
data-bus, and divider-busy holds retain the existing priority rules.
An actual EX recovery overrides instruction-bus/load-use holds, but
is suppressed while EX is held behind a stalled memory operation.
Train exactly once per eligible EX advance, never on reset, bubbles,
repeated held instructions, or unfinished division. Invalidate a tag
hit resolving as a non-control or otherwise ineligible instruction;
stale or aliased targets must always be corrected before younger work
can execute. For divide instructions, stale-prediction recovery occurs
only when the completed divide is accepted, without losing its captured
operands or retirement payload. Keep predictor ports inline in existing
modules so all explicit RTL source lists remain valid.

Preserve nret=1, all top-level IO, decoder legality, registered division,
forwarding, exactly-once memory side effects, and retirement ordering.
Judge the proposal by unchanged formal/cosim gates and median Gowin Fmax
times bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle with the existing bus stalls.
The prior cycle reduction would give approximately 6.7% fitness gain
at unchanged Fmax. With the previous 4,208,674-cycle result as an estimate,
median Fmax must exceed approximately 43.36 MHz to beat the champion by
more than 4.6%, allowing only about a 2% frequency loss. The
timing-conscious recovery aims to preserve or improve clock frequency.
These are expectations, not new RTL or timing measurements.

title: Separate the memory address register from the general ALU result
motivation:
The champion scores 113.27 at 47.673 MHz with 4,208,611 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported 26.427 ns worst path starts at the
register file, crosses ID, EX and the general ALU, and ends at data
memory. Prior micro_opt work on redirect payload masking changed
fitness by only 0.01 percent; registering recovery added cycles and
regressed. The current memory stage drives its address from the same
EX/MEM alu_result used for every integer and multiply result. This
unnecessarily connects the full ALU result selection to the memory
address endpoint, although legal loads and stores always use rs1+imm.
A fresh unchanged-RTL Gowin option-0 run reproduced 47.320 MHz and
that path; its detailed report includes a multiplier DSP followed
by eight LUT levels on the route to a data-memory address pin.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce a dedicated effective-address datapath and EX/MEM address
register for loads and stores, retaining every existing pipeline
boundary and instruction latency. In EX compute a 32-bit modulo sum
of the fully forwarded rs1 and the registered immediate independently
of ALU operand selection, the ALU operation mux, jump-link selection,
and division-result selection. Capture this address in a separate
EX/MEM field with the same reset and data-memory hold enable as the
instruction it accompanies. The existing alu_result stays responsible
for arithmetic writeback and nonload forwarding.

Drive the memory address, access-alignment checks, byte-lane masks,
load extraction and RVFI aligned memory address from this dedicated
field. For valid memory instructions the new address must equal the
old ALU_ADD result exactly, including wraparound and every forwarded
operand source. When no memory transaction is active, the bus address
may expose the registered sum; continue to qualify read and write
enables by instruction validity, reset and misalignment. Do not put
a general-ALU-result fallback mux on the memory address output.

Keep address capture independent of division completion and of jump
result selection. If a division payload or bubble is emitted, the
address is irrelevant because its memory enables are zero. During
data-bus backpressure, address, data and masks remain stable with the
held EX/MEM instruction, and older WB forwarding remains available.
Preserve the current load-use interlock, predictor, multicycle divider,
decoder legality, ALTOPS formulas and nret=1 top-level contract.

This is one local datapath specialization, with no new execution
stage, cache or predictor changes. The proposed benefit is a shorter
arithmetic-to-memory cone and less fanout on the general ALU result.
CoreMark cycles should be unchanged; at that cycle count, acceptance
requires median Gowin Fmax above about 49.87 MHz. Estimate an 8 percent
fitness gain with medium confidence. A different writeback, multiply
or predictor path may become critical, and synthesis may share the
address addition with the ordinary ADD implementation. Timing benefit
must therefore be measured in the unchanged vendor flow.

Require the existing formal, unit and stalled cosim gates and canonical
CoreMark CRCs. Add directed address tests for EX/MEM and retained WB
forwarding, immediate load/store dependence, negative offsets,
carry propagation, every byte lane and halfword alignment, misaligned
traps, older memory stalls and divide completion. Check actual memory
transaction addresses and masks, exactly-once stores, RVFI memory
fields, retirement order, and unchanged bracketed cycles. This file
proposes an implementation for the orchestrator to build and verify.

A temporary RTL prototype used one independent 32-bit address register,
reset to zero and otherwise capturing forwarded rs1+imm whenever
!stall, and overlaid it on the EX/MEM output bundle. Every memory-stage
address consumer used the new field; general alu_result writeback
remained unchanged. Vendor builds measured 52.292, 51.569 and 51.569 MHz
for placement options 0, 1 and 2, respectively, a 51.569 MHz median.

approximately 122.53 iterations/second if its 4,208,611 measured cycles
are retained. Logic changed from 3364 to 3318, registers from 874 to
906, and LUT-RAM/BSRAM/DSP counts stayed 52/6/6. The option-0 worst path
moved from a data-memory address to the ordinary ALU-result register
and shortened from 26.427 to 24.418 ns. The temporary prototype also
passed all 27 existing cocotb pipeline tests under Verilator, including
load/store forwarding, memory holds, division and predictor recovery.

fitness result; full formal, additional directed memory checks and
bracketed CoreMark validation remain required.

title: Split execute into fast and registered completion paths
motivation:
The champion's 47.673 MHz median Fmax and fitness 113.27 are limited
by two long execute cones. A fresh Gowin option-0 build reproduces
47.320 MHz: the worst path crosses a combinational DSP multiplier
after forwarding, while another nearly equal path passes through
the JALR adder, target checking, and frontend recovery. The successful
structural divider attempt isolated deep arithmetic; the failed
registered-recovery attempt added about 8% cycles without lifting
the arithmetic ceiling. This favors selectively registering long
execution operations while retaining current conditional-branch
and direct-jump latency.

Scratch experiments directly support this execution split.
Registering multiplication alone reached 50.676 MHz in option 0
but left JALR recovery critical and barely repaid its extra cycles.
The combined registered multiply/JALR prototype reaches 56.447,
58.074, and 58.074 MHz across Gowin placement options 0, 1, and 2,
giving median Fmax 58.074 MHz. It uses 3,732 logic cells, 1,041
registers, 52 LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs, and two DSP blocks. It passes
all 27 existing pipeline tests and the unchanged stalled CoreMark
UART/CRC validator with no out-of-bounds accesses. These are scratch
measurements, not a completed formal gate or accepted tournament run.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one structural split between fast EX execution and a
blocking registered completion path. Route MUL, MULH, MULHU,
MULHSU, and JALR through completion registers, using the existing
divider's hold-and-drain discipline. Ordinary RV32I ALU operations,
conditional branches, and JAL retain their current latency.
Preserve the predictor, memory protocol, decoder legality,
alignment traps, divider arithmetic, and nret=1 port contract.
This selectively cuts both measured long cones rather than adding
a stage to every instruction or delaying every branch recovery.

Remove the three combinational full-product networks from alu.sv.
Share one multiplier with unsigned 16-by-16 partial products.
At launch, register p00=a[15:0]*b[15:0], p01=a[15:0]*b[31:16],
p10=a[31:16]*b[15:0], and p11=a[31:16]*b[31:16], each explicitly
32 bits wide, and capture original fully forwarded a, b, opcode,
and complete retirement metadata on that same edge. On the next
edge register the selected result, then consume it into EX/MEM
on the following accepted edge. This costs two extra issue cycles
per multiply; avoid an additional operand-only capture stage.

Reconstruct the exact 64-bit product as p00 + (p01 << 16)
+ (p10 << 16) + (p11 << 32), widening every term before shifting.
MUL selects its low word, MULHU its high word. MULH subtracts b
from the unsigned high word when a[31] is set and subtracts a
when b[31] is set; MULHSU applies only the first correction.
Reduce products and corrections with a carry-save tree and one
final carry-propagate adder. Incorporate each high-word subtraction
as a complemented operand shifted by 32 plus its bit-32 carry-in,
avoiding serial carry-propagate sign corrections. Arithmetic is
modulo 2^64, with selected high words modulo 2^32. Hold the final
registered result until consumed. Retain the four exact existing
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS multiply formulas through the same capture/
completion interface with short bounded latency; real simulation
and synthesis use multiplication.

For JALR, register fully forwarded rs1+imm at launch, clearing
bit 0 and capturing original operands, link PC+4, PC, instruction,
prediction metadata, and target-alignment fault. Hold ID/EX for
one extra issue cycle. Prediction target checking, frontend
recovery, and predictor training use the registered target
exclusively at completion. The raw JALR adder must terminate at
its target register, with no combinational shortcut to recovery.
At launch, construct captured retirement data and fault handling
from the newly computed target, not a previous target-register
value. A target with bit 1 set traps, suppresses the link write
and redirect, and preserves existing fall-through reporting.
Correctly predicted JALRs also pay the one-cycle execution hold.
Keep conditional-branch and JAL resolution on their current path.

Use one pending-instruction payload/completion discipline in EX;
only one blocking instruction is in flight, so existing divider
payload storage can be reused where practical. Launch once for
a valid unstalled instruction and capture forwarded values once
before older WB writers drain. Hold fetch and ID/EX while pending.
Let older MEM/WB work drain and write fully zeroed EX/MEM bubbles
whenever that register is free; preserve an older stalled memory
request. A completed result remains pending across actual downstream
backpressure and transfers exactly once, without relaunch, loss,
duplicate retirement, or repeated memory effects. An unrelated
low dmemReady need not block multiply/JALR completion when EX/MEM
can advance. Preserve existing division acceptance behavior.
Reset cancels pending work. Gate training and stale-prediction
recovery on final instruction advance, including multiply recovery.
RVFI reports captured operands and actual successors with strictly
contiguous channel-0 retirement order.

The timed instruction profile has 93,960 multiplies and 13,735
JALRs among 2,922,015 instructions. The combined scratch cosim
measures 4,409,538 bracketed cycles versus the champion's 4,208,611:
4.77% overhead with the existing instruction/data bus stalls.
All five canonical CRCs and the required validation literal match.
Median 58.074 MHz times 10/4,409,538 iterations/cycle gives fitness
about 131.7, approximately 16.3% above 113.27. With this cycle count,
median Fmax must exceed approximately 52.25 MHz to clear the 4.6%
acceptance margin. Final implementation still requires unchanged

title: Decouple predicted fetch with a compact four-entry flow-through queue
motivation:
The champion's 32-entry tagged bimodal predictor already reduces bracketed
CoreMark cycles to 4,208,611 and reaches 113.27 fitness at 47.673 MHz.
A fresh canonical CoreMark reference trace reproduces 73,619 remaining
predictor recoveries over 2,922,016 timed instructions. Even eliminating
every remaining recovery would save less than 2% of cycles, below the
4.6% acceptance margin. Temporary vendor timing probes of narrower or
smaller BTBs did not improve clock frequency, so accuracy or storage
changes alone have weak prospects. The current predicted-fetch PC also
stops on every backend load-use, data-bus, and divider hold, wasting
available instruction-bus cycles even though future PCs are predicted.
Its timed IPC is about 0.694, below the approximately 0.78 instruction-bus
acceptance ceiling, leaving room to overlap fetch and backend stalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the champion's 32-entry full-tag bimodal BTB and its timing-conscious
EX recovery unchanged, but let predicted fetch run independently into a
four-entry flow-through queue. This is one predictor-front-end change:
use predicted successors to fetch ahead during backend interlocks and
consume buffered instructions during subsequent instruction-bus stalls.
Each queued entry stores the instruction, prediction-selected bit, and
full predicted target. Track its full architectural fetch PC with one
separate dequeue-PC register instead of four stored PC words. Never synthesize an
instruction from predictor state or reuse a bus word that was not
accepted with imemReady high.

Use an occupancy counter ranging from zero to four and four payload
registers. When the
queue is nonempty, present its oldest entry to ID independent of current
imemReady. When empty, present the raw current bus instruction and lookup
metadata combinationally, allowing direct acceptance on the same edge as
today. A ready instruction that bypasses into ID advances the predicted
fetch PC without entering the queue. If ID is held, enqueue an accepted
bus instruction and advance the predicted fetch PC while space remains.
A full queue can accept a replacement on the same edge its head is
consumed. For simultaneous dequeue/enqueue, shift the surviving oldest
payload correctly and preserve FIFO order. Without bus readiness there
is no enqueue or ordinary fetch-PC advance, but a buffered head may still
enter ID. Without backend acceptance there is no dequeue. An empty,
unavailable bus supplies an invalid ID bubble as in the champion.

Initialize both fetch PC and dequeue PC to RESET_PC, and replace both
with the resolved target on recovery. Advance dequeue PC only when ID
actually accepts a valid queue head or empty-queue bypass: use that
instruction's saved predicted target if prediction-selected is set,
otherwise dequeue PC plus four. Because every accepted bus word follows
exactly this predicted successor sequence, this reconstructs each full
queued PC without truncation. Export the dequeue PC as out.pc; do not
expose the ahead-running fetch PC as the buffered instruction's PC.
Queue metadata remains a snapshot, so later training cannot change this
PC sequence. The four-entry representation saves 96 PC-storage bits
compared with four complete PC payloads, accounting for the one added
32-bit dequeue-PC register. Keep full 32-bit targets and PCs everywhere.

Repurpose the frontend hold from the hazard unit to mean backend cannot
consume: load-use, an older stalled memory operation, or execute_busy.
Remove instruction-bus readiness from that consumption hold; the fetch
stage itself qualifies bus acceptance. Load-use detection uses the
presented queue-head instruction and validity, never raw bus bits when
a different instruction is buffered. Preserve existing ID flush/hold,
MEM/WB retention, and EX/MEM stall priorities. Do not buffer decoded
register values: ID must read the live regfile when the instruction
actually leaves the queue, preserving WB bypass and EX forwarding.

On an eligible EX prediction mismatch, recovery has priority over queue
activity and frontend holds: flush all entries, discard any same-edge
bus acceptance, suppress head acceptance, and install the full resolved
target PC. Correct predictions do not flush the queue. Reset clears
occupancy and resets the PC. Keep raw head/bypass payload selection and
predictor lookup independent of redirect; qualify validity separately,
preserving the existing protection against redirect-to-instruction and
source-address combinational feedback. Capture prediction metadata at
bus acceptance and hold it unchanged until ID accepts that instruction;
later BTB updates must not rewrite queued metadata. Train only on the
existing once-per-EX-advance event, never on queue enqueue/dequeue alone.
Preserve stale-entry checks for every advancing instruction, misaligned
transfer traps, and divide-completion recovery. Speculative instructions
cannot reach EX or memory after a recovery flush. Avoid speculative
lookahead beyond the platform's executable RAM boundary; maintain the
full-width architectural fallback and recovery behavior.

Flow-through when empty preserves the champion's zero-wait fetch and
recovery latency. The proposed gain comes from using otherwise idle
instruction-bus opportunities and amortizing later fetch stalls, not
extra retirement width or different arithmetic. At unchanged Fmax a
6% fitness gain requires about 3.970 million bracketed cycles; the 4.6%
acceptance threshold requires fewer than about 4.024 million. The
approximately 0.78 fetch-bandwidth ceiling permits up to about 12%
improvement over current IPC, before backend and recovery costs. Queue
muxing and added wrong-path work can reduce those gains or Fmax, so the
proposal must be judged by median Gowin timing and canonical stalled
CoreMark cycles together. A temporary four-entry full-PC probe measured
3,983,322 bracketed cycles, canonical CRCs and validation UART, no OOB,
and median Fmax 46.571 MHz: about 116.91 fitness, a 3.2% gain that misses
acceptance. Thus buffering has a measured cycle benefit, while reducing
queue storage and preserving timing is necessary to clear the margin.
The compact four-entry prototype then measured the same 3,983,322 cycles
and median Fmax 48.745 MHz across placement options [45.535, 48.745,
48.745], yielding 122.37 fitness, about 8.0% above the champion. It used
3,736 LUT4 and 1,161 FF, and produced the canonical CRCs, validation UART,
and no OOB. Results are temporary exploratory artifacts under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/queue_4_compact/result.json;
reimplement and rerun all unchanged evaluator gates for acceptance.
These exploratory probes are not a completed formal-gated candidate.
Preserve nret=1, external IO, all legality and
arithmetic checks, RVFI resolved PCs/order, and every evaluation gate.

title: Precompute forwarding matches and flatten EX operand selection
motivation:
The champion scores 131.70 at median Gowin Fmax 58.072 MHz and
4,409,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at the
EX/MEM destination tag, crosses forwarding and EX operand selection,
then the fast ALU and data memory: 26 cells, 24.558 ns. Registered
MUL/JALR removed their competing timing cones, making ordinary bypass
selection a worthwhile remaining target. The prior micro_opt attempts
shared the combinational divider, removed validity-driven payload
masking, or separated memory addresses; none precomputed bypass tag
matches. Their results and the failed delayed-recovery experiment
favor a local timing change that preserves instruction cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize the existing forwarding network as one local control and
operand-selection change: compute its destination/source tag matches
during ID, register four match bits alongside ID/EX, then select EX
operands using priority-qualified one-hot enables and flat masked ORs.
Preserve the pipeline boundaries and every instruction latency.

Add four ID/EX fields: EX-match and WB-match for each source. On the
same edge that ID accepts an instruction, compare its raw rs1/rs2
fields against the CURRENT ID/EX rd and CURRENT EX/MEM rd respectively,
including rd != 0 in each comparison. The former producer advances
into EX/MEM at that edge; the latter advances into MEM/WB. Therefore
the registered matches correspond to the producer stages supplying
the consumer's following EX cycle. Wire these two older destination
tags into id_stage; do not compare against the current MEM/WB tag.
Capture matches under exactly the same acceptance condition as the
consumer's other ID/EX fields, and reset/flush/bubble/hold them with
that payload. Do not register a speculative reg_write qualification:
misalignment traps can suppress the actual producer's write later.

In EX forwarding, qualify the saved EX-match with the existing live
ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write, and the saved WB-match with
mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write. Retain WB eligibility WITHOUT mem_wb.valid:
memory stalls clear only retirement valid while preserving the
preceding WB value needed by a held consumer. For each source define
E and W as these qualified matches, and export a three-bit mask with
bit 0 selecting ID/EX, bit 1 EX/MEM and bit 2 WB:
{(!E && W), E, (!E && !W)}. EX/MEM wins if both match; exactly one
source is selected. Remove the EX-stage five-bit tag comparisons and
binary selector encoding/decoding from this path.

Form architectural forwarded rs1/rs2 as the OR of the three source
words ANDed with replicated mask bits. Separately flatten ALU source
selection into that same network: A selects PC with is_auipc or the
three rs1 sources with !is_auipc && their masks; B selects imm with
alu_src or the three rs2 sources with !alu_src && their masks.
Qualify the one-bit enables before replicating across data bits, and
use explicit parallel AND/OR expressions. Do not place a PC/immediate
mux after an already selected forwarded value. Raw forwarded rs1/rs2
must still drive branch comparisons, stores, JALR launch and RVFI
operands; immediate-selected ALU B must never become store data.

During an older dmem hold, ID/EX and EX/MEM stay fixed and MEM/WB
retains its data, so the saved matches remain associated with the
same producers. During a blocking MUL/DIV/JALR, older stages may drain
and those matches may become stale, but the existing pending payload
and arithmetic units already capture all forwarded operands ONCE at
launch. Preserve that capture and never reread held ID/EX operands
to construct a completion. At final acceptance, compute the next
consumer's matches using the completing instruction's held rd and
the current EX/MEM rd. Retain the current load-use bubble, recovery,
reset, drain-bubble and exactly-once completion priorities. Gate
forwarding with actual stage write controls so misaligned or illegal
producers cannot supply a result.

Keep ALU arithmetic, multiplier/divider real and ALTOPS branches,
decoder legality, predictor, memory handshakes, misalignment traps,
RVFI order and operands, and nret=1 top-level IO unchanged. No new
execution stage, added branch penalty, memory-address register or
benchmark-specific specialization is part of this hypothesis.

A temporary prototype of this exact combination measured Gowin Fmax
[56.571, 61.748, 61.748] MHz across placement options 0/1/2, giving
61.748 MHz median: 6.33 percent above the champion. An independent
untouched-RTL rerun reproduced [51.912, 58.072, 58.072] MHz exactly.
Prototype option-0 resources were 3,942 LUT4 and 1,105 FF versus
3,910 LUT4 and 1,111 FF; LUT-RAM/BSRAM/DSP stayed 52/6/2. Its worst
path moved off the forwarding destination tag to the regfile data
path, shortened to 22.972 ns, and crossed 15 cells. Thus the measured
gain accompanies a changed timing cone, rather than a neutral edit.

The prototype passed all 32 existing pipeline cases and both direct
EX cases, retaining their assertions while adapting EX port masks
and packed ID/EX layout. Full RVFI cosim passed selftest plus all
three random instruction programs both with zero waits and with
simultaneous instruction/data stalls. Canonical 2K, -O3, ITERATIONS=10
CoreMark with both stall streams completed with the five expected
CRCs, validation UART, no OOB and exactly 4,409,538 bracketed cycles.
This implies exploratory fitness 140.03, a 6.33 percent increase,
exceeding the 4.6 percent threshold. Results are under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/early_onehot/; these ignored
artifacts will be deleted by the orchestrator and are not deliverables.
Reimplement the described RTL and rerun all unchanged evaluation gates,
especially formal, before acceptance; formal was not run on this probe.

title: Register one-hot forwarding provenance ahead of execute
motivation:
The current champion reaches 58.072 MHz and fitness 131.70 after
registering multiplication and JALR completion. Its reported worst path
now starts at an EX/MEM destination-register tag and crosses forward_unit,
the EX operand muxes, the ordinary ALU, and the memory interface. This
makes producer matching and bypass selection the next structural target.
Earlier blanket branch recovery registration added about 8% CoreMark
cycles without removing the arithmetic ceiling; the fetch FIFO also lost
to the selective execution split. Retiming forwarding control offers a
timing improvement without deliberately adding instruction latency.

The current champion reaches 58.072 MHz and fitness 131.70 after
registering multiplication and JALR completion. Its reported worst path
now starts at an EX/MEM destination-register tag and crosses forward_unit,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move source-versus-producer matching across the ID/EX clock boundary.
Resolve the next EX instruction's operand provenance during decode and
register its two one-hot forwarding selections alongside the instruction.
Keep these as two three-bit registers in core.sv at the ID/EX boundary,
leaving the packed instruction bundle unchanged, as in the prototype.
Encode base=001, EX/MEM=010, and MEM/WB=100, resolving youngest-writer
priority before the register. EX forms each operand as the bitwise OR
of the three data candidates masked by their registered source bits;
do not reintroduce an encoded-select decoder or priority mux in EX.
Eliminate live destination-tag comparators and priority resolution from
the EX-to-ALU path. Preserve
EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority and x0 behavior, the existing ALU and memory
register boundaries, and the current fast branch/JAL latency.

Compute selections against the producers that will actually occupy
EX/MEM and MEM/WB after the same edge, rather than against their current
positions. Expose the effective next-state destination and forwarding
enable from EX and MEM, including bubbles, held data, completed blocking
operations, and write suppression on alignment traps. For EX, derive
this metadata from the actual EX/MEM next-state payload: retained on
memory hold, captured pending payload on consume, zero on blocking drain,
or the normal execution payload. Eligibility is next valid AND next
reg_write. For MEM, use the held WB destination/control on hold, otherwise
the incoming destination and alignment-corrected reg_write. Preserve the
incumbent forwarding eligibility of retained WB fields independently
of WB valid. For normal decode
acceptance, match fetched source addresses to those next-state producers.
Reset and flush select base=001; invalid instruction validity continues
to suppress execution and all side effects. Recompute selection registers
on every non-reset, non-flush edge. Use the held ID/EX source addresses
when stall_id is asserted without flush_id; otherwise use fetched source
addresses. This refreshes provenance when a producer moves from EX/MEM
to MEM/WB. On each ID/EX hold without flush, also capture EX's currently
forwarded rs1 and rs2 into the held instruction's base operand fields,
preserving a source after its producer leaves the bypass window.
Keep retained WB
data eligible for forwarding during dmem stalls even when WB valid is
cleared, while actual writes and retirement still require valid.

Keep load-use bubbling and all older-memory hold priorities unchanged.
Blocking MUL, DIV, REM, and JALR capture their fully forwarded operands
once at launch and continue using their existing pending payloads and
completion handshakes. Their consume edge must correctly describe the
producer entering EX/MEM for a newly accepted dependent instruction.
Redirect flushes, predictor training, reset cancellation, exact-once
memory transactions, contiguous channel-0 RVFI retirement, decoder
default-illegal behavior, real M arithmetic and ALTOPS formulas, and
the nret=1 external port contract remain intact. This is one forwarding
control retiming change; do not add a general operand pipeline stage or
combine it with predictor, cache, or evaluation changes.

A scratch implementation of this retiming with encoded controls reached
median 61.520 MHz; registering one-hot source controls instead reaches
63.473, 62.732, and 62.732 MHz in Gowin placement options 0, 1, and 2,
respectively, for median 62.732 MHz. Its option-0 area is 3,927 logic
cells, 1,084 registers, 52 LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs, and two DSP blocks.
The one-hot prototype passes all six existing cocotb unit runners,
including 32 pipeline tests; only the EX unit test's driven source codes
were adapted to the new encoding, with every assertion retained.
It passes the unchanged selftest and three random-program instruction
cosims with and without bus stalls, and validates all five canonical
CoreMark CRCs and the required UART literal with no out-of-bounds access.
It preserves exactly 4,409,538 bracketed cycles for ten iterations.
The one-hot prototype also passes all 53 unchanged fast formal checks,
including register consistency, illegal instructions, order, and
liveness. At unchanged
cycles, 62.732 MHz projects to fitness about 142.26, an 8.0% gain over
131.70; the 4.6% acceptance threshold requires about 60.74 MHz.
These are prototype measurements and a projection, not an accepted
tournament result. Main risks are stale selections during backpressure
and a competing regfile-data/ALU path limiting final implementation
timing after the producer-control path is cut.

Retain all existing checks. Add directed EX/MEM and WB dependencies,
simultaneous writers to one register, x0, load-use, held WB forwarding,
long bus stalls, blocking-operation completion dependencies, illegal
and misaligned writers, and redirect/reset cases. Verify exact operand
values and results, RVFI order, PCs, and exactly-once memory effects.

followed by the evaluator's median Gowin Fmax times bracketed iterations

title: Buffer predicted fetch across the champion's execute holds
motivation:
The current champion already has a tagged bimodal predictor and registered
MUL/JALR completion, but fetch still stops on every load-use, data-memory,
and execute-busy hold. This wastes ready instruction-bus opportunities and
leaves later instruction stalls uncovered. Improving direction accuracy
alone is unlikely to exceed the 4.6% acceptance margin: the earlier trace
estimate found only 73,619 remaining recoveries among roughly 4.2 million
cycles. The previous four-entry predicted-fetch queue reduced its parent's
measured cycles from 4,208,611 to 3,983,322, a 5.35% reduction, and improved
that parent's fitness by 6.91%. It lost the tournament to registered
MUL/JALR, rather than demonstrating that buffering cannot improve that
newer core. Apply the frontend change to the present 58.072 MHz,
4,409,538-cycle champion, preserving its registered arithmetic and
indirect-target timing boundaries. The additional execute holds provide
further opportunities to fetch ahead. An isolated four-entry probe on
this exact base now measures 4,053,425 bracketed cycles and 57.275 MHz
median Gowin Fmax, or 141.30 fitness, 7.29% above the champion. A fresh
baseline run reproduces 4,409,538 cycles with the same canonical ELF.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple the existing predicted fetch stream from backend acceptance with
one compact four-entry flow-through instruction queue. Keep the current
32-entry tagged BTB, two-bit counters, EX recovery, and registered
multiplier/divider/JALR completion intact. This is a single frontend
hypothesis: use already predicted successors to collect accepted bus
instructions during backend holds, then supply them during instruction
stalls. Do not combine it with a new direction predictor or a cache.

Separate bus acceptance from ID acceptance. A nonempty queue presents
its oldest instruction independently of current imemReady. An empty
queue bypasses the raw bus instruction and lookup metadata directly to
ID, retaining the champion's zero-wait latency. Accept an instruction
from the bus only with imemReady and available capacity; advance the
fetch PC along its snapshotted predicted successor only on acceptance.
If ID accepts an empty-queue bypass, do not also enqueue it. If ID is
held, enqueue it while capacity remains. Support simultaneous pop/push,
including replacement of a full queue's consumed head, without duplicate
instructions, skipped PCs, or reordered entries. With no ready bus and
an empty queue, present an invalid bubble. When the queue cannot accept,
hold the outstanding fetch PC and do not reuse an unaccepted bus word.
Use a three-bit occupancy count from zero to four. Pop only a nonempty
consumed head; push only an accepted bus instruction that did not bypass
into ID. On pop, shift surviving entries toward the head; append a push
at old_count minus pop. Only push changes occupancy by +1, only pop by
-1, and simultaneous push/pop leaves occupancy unchanged.

Store four instruction words, four prediction-selected bits, and four
full aligned predicted targets. Reconstruct queued instruction PCs with
one full-width dequeue-PC register: advance it only when ID accepts a
valid head or bypass, using that entry's saved selected target or PC+4.
Initialize both fetch and dequeue PCs to zero and replace both on EX
recovery. This preserves the exact accepted predicted-PC sequence while
saving three PC words relative to a full-PC queue. Predictor training
must never rewrite queued metadata. ID reads the live regfile when the
head is consumed; do not queue decoded operand values. Preserve every
full architectural PC and target bit and the existing stale-prediction
checks, including ordinary instructions and traps.

Make the IF hold input describe backend consumption holds: load-use,
older dmem backpressure, and execute_busy. Handle instruction-bus
readiness locally in IF instead of including it in this consumption
hold. The hazard unit must inspect the presented head's instruction
and validity. Preserve ID flush/hold priorities, EX/MEM memory holds,
retained MEM/WB forwarding data, and all registered completion behavior.
Queue activity must not feed new combinational logic into the forwarded
ALU, branch comparison, or registered JALR target computation.

A real EX recovery overrides frontend holds, clears all queued younger
work, discards same-edge bus acceptance, suppresses ID acceptance, and
installs the resolved full target. A correctly predicted transfer keeps
the queue. Keep raw head/bypass selection and BTB lookup independent of
redirect, qualifying validity separately so recovery does not create a
source-address feedback path. Train only on the existing once-per-final-
EX-advance event, including MUL/DIV/JALR completion; never on enqueue,
dequeue, or a held instruction. Reset cancels all queued work. Respect
the executable-memory boundary when running ahead without truncating
architectural PCs or preventing demand fetch and recovery progress.

The expected benefit is reduced bracketed cycles on the current base,
with median Gowin Fmax near the champion's. At unchanged Fmax, acceptance
requires fewer than 4,215,620 cycles; a 7% gain requires approximately
4,121,064 cycles. A 5.35% cycle reduction would leave only about 1% Fmax
loss before missing acceptance, so avoid adding queue control to EX or
growing predictor lookup logic. The temporary combined prototype saves
8.08% of cycles while losing 1.37% of median Fmax, clearing the margin
in this exploratory run. Placement options [0, 1, 2] measure
[53.639, 57.275, 57.275] MHz; option-0 area is 4,310 LUT4 and 1,398 FF,
with the champion's two DSPs. The unchanged harness reports all canonical
CoreMark CRCs, the validation UART literal, both timing markers, and no
OOB. Full RVFI comparisons against the unchanged ISS pass selftest and
all three random programs, each with zero waits and with both random bus
stalls, eight runs total. This probe lives under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/queue4_current and leaves the
champion RTL unchanged. It is not a completed formal-gated candidate:
reimplement from this hypothesis and run all unchanged unit, formal,
cosim, and FPGA gates. Speculative-boundary handling and directed
FIFO/reset tests still require implementation validation. Score the
actual median vendor Fmax times bracketed iterations/cycle, preserving
nret=1, decoder legality, arithmetic, resolved RVFI PCs/order, and all
existing correctness checks.

title: Preserve fast operand delivery with distributed register RAM and registered writeback selection
motivation:
The champion scores 144.84 at median Gowin Fmax 63.869 MHz with
4,409,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior micro_opt attempts addressed
division, bubble masking, memory-address separation, and forwarding;
none controlled register-file memory inference and writeback-data
placement together. A fresh unchanged option-0 run reproduces
60.645 MHz and the 21.784 ns worst path. Detailed vendor timing shows
register-file block RAM launching both limiting execute paths, with
2.260 ns clock-to-Q. Replacing it with flops alone merely exposes the
WB load/ALU mux and does not improve median Fmax. Distributed RAM alone
also exposes that mux. These competing paths motivate one focused
operand-delivery optimization: preserve the existing ID operand-capture
boundary with asynchronous distributed register RAM, and select the
final WB value before its register rather than on the EX bypass path.

placement together. A fresh unchanged option-0 run reproduces

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the existing pipeline and instruction timing, but restructure
register-file and writeback operand delivery so EX sources come from
explicitly registered values without a block-RAM output or late
load-versus-ALU selection. Both parts address the same operand-delivery
cone; do not change arithmetic, prediction, fetch buffering, or issue
policy.

In reg_file, infer the 32-by-32 array as asynchronous distributed RAM
using Gowin's supported syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram" attribute. Keep
the single synchronous write and both combinational reads. Remove the
bulk reset of stored RAM data, which prevents the desired inference,
and replace it with a resettable 32-bit written_q vector. Reset clears
all written bits and suppresses the RAM write; a normal enabled write
to x1..x31 sets its written bit and stores all 32 data bits. A read of
an unwritten register returns zero, making architectural reset behavior
identical even though stale physical RAM contents remain. Preserve the
exact existing priorities: x0 always reads zero; otherwise a same-cycle
enabled matching write returns w_data; otherwise a written register
returns its RAM word, and an unwritten register returns zero. Writes
to x0 are ignored. A later reset must hide every prior stored word
until it is written again. Keep ports and full address/data widths.
The asynchronous read feeds the existing ID/EX operand capture; do
not add a read cycle or change the registered forwarding provenance.

Add a wb_data field to mem_wb_t. At ordinary MEM/WB capture register
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result into this field, after
the existing load alignment and sign/zero extension. Reset clears it;
during hold_wb retain it together with the other data fields while
clearing retirement valid exactly as today. wb_stage's w_data becomes
a direct wire from this registered field. Preserve its w_en and
w_addr, the effective next-WB forwarding metadata, and the retained
WB-data eligibility after valid clears. Existing alu_result/read_data
fields may remain for compatibility; remove their combinational
writeback selection from the timed operand path. This moves selection
across an existing register boundary, with no new stage or extra cycle.

Keep decoder legality, real and ALTOPS arithmetic, predictor training
and recovery, held-operand refresh, load-use bubbles, MUL/DIV/JALR
capture/completion, dmem handshakes, traps, RVFI order and operands,
and nret=1 top-level IO unchanged. Do not alter evaluation sources or
force placement. Use the RAM inference attribute only for the desired
storage primitive, without keep/dont_touch directives.

An isolated probe of this combined structure measures 65.265 MHz on
Gowin placement option 0 versus the reproduced 60.645 MHz base,
a 7.62 percent gain. Worst arrival shortens from 21.784 to 20.617 ns;
the critical launch moves off register-file RAM and WB selection to
registered forwarding controls. Resources are 4,237 LUTs, 1,064 FF,
76 LUT-RAMs, 4 BSRAMs, and 2 DSPs, versus 3,998/1,084/52/6/2 for the
base. Both register-file BSRAMs disappear, without the large flop
increase of the unsuccessful explicit-register implementation.
All three vendor placements complete at [65.265, 67.366, 67.366]
MHz, for a 67.366 MHz median. With the identical measured CoreMark
cycles, exploratory fitness is 152.77 iterations/second: 5.48 percent
above the 144.84 champion, exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
This is prototype timing and simulation evidence, not a formal-gated
acceptance result. The narrow margin makes faithful reconstruction and
all three vendor placements necessary.

The probe passes all five register-file tests and all 38 pipeline
tests. Full RVFI comparisons pass selftest and three random programs,
each with zero waits and with both random bus-stall streams, eight
runs total. Stalled canonical CoreMark reports all five expected CRCs,
the validation UART literal, both timing markers, no OOB, and exactly
4,409,538 bracketed cycles. Probe RTL and reports reside under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/lutram_wb/; they are ignored
experimental evidence, not implementation deliverables. Reimplement
from this description and require all unchanged evaluation gates,
including formal, which has not been run on the probe. At unchanged
cycles acceptance needs median Fmax above approximately 66.807 MHz.
Routing of the written-bit mux and the next recovery/control path
remain uncertainties; judge actual median vendor Fmax times measured
iterations/cycle, not individual placement results or RVFI pruning.

title: Preserve decode operand flops with a flop-bank register file
motivation:
The champion reaches 63.869 MHz and fitness 144.84 with 4,409,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Earlier structural changes successfully
isolated division, multiply/JALR completion, and forwarding control;
delayed branch recovery and fetch buffering did not beat their cost.
A fresh unchanged Gowin option-0 build reproduces 60.645 MHz. Its worst
paths start at the register-file memory's CLKB-to-DO output and pass
directly through EX forwarding and the ordinary ALU. The synthesized
register-file read has absorbed the intended ID/EX operand register,
exposing memory clock-to-output latency on the execute critical path.
This offers a register-boundary improvement without adding issue cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild only the integer register-file storage and its existing decode
operand capture as an explicit flip-flop bank with a balanced read tree,
preventing Gowin from absorbing ID/EX operand flops into a RAM read port.
Store x1 through x31 in separately elaborated 32-bit word registers with
synchronous reset and decoded write enables. Make x0 constant zero.
Use two one-hot source decoders and independent balanced AND/OR read
trees over these words, rather than variable-index reads of an inferred
memory. The tested topology uses two 63-node binary trees: leaf 31+i
holds word i masked by its corresponding source-address comparison;
leaf 31 is constant zero for x0. Internal nodes 0 through 30 OR children
2*i+1 and 2*i+2, giving five balanced reduction levels. Each x1-x31
word is declared locally inside its own generate block and reset/write
always_ff, with a constant-index read-tree leaf assignment. Keep the
register-file interface combinational and preserve
same-cycle WB write-first bypass, then capture each read value in the
existing ID/EX operand flops. No additional pipeline stage or ordinary
dependency bubble is intended. This is one structural register-file
implementation change; retain the existing pipeline topology, ALU,
predictor, registered one-hot EX forwarding and blocking M/JALR units.

The desired circuit has two bounded paths: word flops through a balanced
read tree and WB bypass to ID/EX operand flops, then operand flops through
existing EX forwarding and ALU to EX/MEM. Inspect vendor timing to verify
the explicit boundary and that RAM CLKB-to-DO no longer starts the EX
operand path. Do not substitute a dont_touch attribute on an otherwise
unchanged inferred memory; the storage and read topology must change.
Use separately generated word registers and explicit tree levels to
avoid memory inference and a serial OR chain. The scratch prototype
changes only reg_file.sv; the incumbent ID/EX operand capture needs no
RTL alteration to become a separate flop boundary with this storage.

Preserve reset-visible zero values, simultaneous independent source
reads, x0 hardwiring, and WB collision behavior. Leave ID/EX flush/hold
priorities and held fully forwarded operand refresh intact. In
particular, producers leaving EX/MEM or WB during data-memory stalls
and MUL/DIV/JALR holds must remain captured in the held base operands.
Keep pending-operation operand capture, load-use bubbling, misalignment
traps, exact-once bus side effects, decoder default-illegal behavior,
and the nret=1 channel-0 RVFI contract unchanged. No M-extension real or
ALTOPS arithmetic changes are needed.

A scratch implementation of precisely this register-file topology
reaches 67.211, 70.604, and 70.604 MHz in vendor placement options
0, 1, and 2, for median 70.604 MHz. Option-0 area is 5,238 logic cells,
2,058 registers, 44 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs, and two DSPs, versus the
champion's 3,998 logic cells, 1,084 registers, 52 LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs,
and two DSPs. The worst paths no longer launch from register-file RAM;
competing WB/EX forwarding and branch-training paths set the new limit.
The prototype passes all six existing cocotb unit runners, all 53
unchanged fast formal checks, and selftest plus three random-program
full instruction cosims both with and without random bus stalls.
The unchanged stalled CoreMark evaluator validates canonical CRCs,
the required UART literal, no out-of-bounds access, and exactly
4,409,538 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. This projects fitness
to 160.12, about 10.5% above 144.84. At unchanged cycles, acceptance
requires median Fmax above approximately 66.81 MHz. These are scratch
prototype measurements and a fitness projection, not an accepted
tournament result. Added flop/read-tree area and different final
routing of WB/EX or branch-training paths remain the main risks.
Require all existing unit, formal, and stalled cosim gates, canonical
CoreMark CRCs/UART, and median vendor timing on the final implementation.
Reject the proposal if it requires extra issue latency or the new read
tree becomes the timing limit before the acceptance margin is reached.

title: Register the predicted fetch stream without a dequeue-PC feedback path
motivation:
The champion already predicts with a 32-entry tagged bimodal BTB. Its
4,409,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles and 63.869 MHz median Fmax produce
144.84 iterations/sec. Prior four-entry predicted-fetch buffering saved
8.08% of those cycles, but achieved only 54.896 MHz and lost fitness.
Its measured worst path ended at u_if/dequeue_pc_q after traversing
forwarding and execute. Reconstructing buffered PCs from each consumed
prediction creates a second successor-selection register controlled by
backend acceptance. A registered queue of complete fetch snapshots can
retain the useful lookahead while removing that added timing cone.
An isolated prototype of this registered full-PC FIFO, including the
frontier guard, measures 4,141,319 bracketed cycles and 63.982 MHz median
vendor Fmax: 154.50 iterations/sec, 6.67% above the champion. Its fresh
parent simulation reproduces the logged 4,409,538 cycles with the same
canonical ELF. These are exploratory measurements, not a completed
formal-gated implementation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace direct combinational fetch-to-decode delivery with one inline
four-entry registered FIFO of complete predicted-fetch snapshots. Each
entry stores full 32-bit PC, instruction, prediction_selected, and full
predicted_target. Keep the existing 32-entry BTB, counter policy,
once-per-final-EX-advance training, registered arithmetic and JALR
completion, and architectural recovery. This is a single predicted
frontend timing hypothesis: make fetch lookahead independent of
backend consumption without reconstructing instruction PCs.

Use independent two-bit read/write pointers and a three-bit occupancy
count. Present only a previously registered oldest entry to ID;
there is no empty-queue combinational bypass. Pop only when nonempty
and ID can consume without a load-use, older-memory, or execute hold.
Push only on imemReady with occupancy less than four at the start of
the cycle. Deliberately do not use same-cycle pop to admit a push into
a full FIFO. Thus fetch-PC ordinary enable and its predicted successor
depend only on registered capacity, bus readiness, and BTB lookup,
never backend pop, load-use detection, or a consumed target.
Simultaneous push/pop at occupancies one through three preserves FIFO
order and count. Pop advances only the read pointer; push advances
only the write pointer and fetch PC. With no push hold the bus address.
Store metadata from the exact accepted bus word, unchanged until pop.
Declare storage as an explicit logic [97:0] entries [0:3] vector array
and assign its selected word into a typed if_id_t head. Use whole-word
packed writes. Yosys rejects dynamic struct-member writes and can
misinterpret an unpacked array declared with the struct typedef, so
do not use that declaration for physical FIFO storage.
Use the queued PC directly as out.pc, eliminating dequeue_pc_q and
every dequeue-side PC+4/target mux. Read live register values at ID
consumption rather than buffering decoded operands.

IF handles raw instruction-bus readiness locally. Remove imemReady
from the hazard unit's backend-consumption hold, and use the presented
FIFO head's instruction and validity for load-use detection. An empty
queue supplies an invalid ID bubble, including the deliberate one-cycle
refill latency after reset or recovery. Keep raw head payload selection
independent of redirect; qualify validity separately as today, so
branch resolution cannot change ID source-register addresses through
a redirect-dependent instruction mux. Normal queue control must not
add logic to the existing EX ALU, branch comparator, or JALR sum.

Reset clears occupancy and pointers and installs RESET_PC. A real
EX recovery has priority over all queue activity and bus holds: flush
all younger snapshots, suppress pop and push on that edge, reset the
pointers, and install the full resolved fetch target. Correctly
predicted transfers retain the FIFO. Do not delay architectural
recovery or weaken stale predictions, ordinary-instruction recovery,
misaligned-target traps, held-operation forwarding, or exactly-once
memory effects. Training remains the existing EX final-advance event,
never a FIFO event. Preserve full-width PCs/targets, nret=1, every
external port, decoder legality, resolved RVFI successors/order, and
all unchanged verification and benchmark contracts.

Bound speculative lookahead without adding a mux to the imem address.
If an accepted word predicts a successor outside [0, 0x00100000),
save that full successor in a frontier_target register, set a wait
bit, and leave the physical fetch PC at the accepted word's address.
While waiting accept no duplicate bus word; already queued work drains
normally. Recovery clears the wait and installs the resolved PC. If
the FIFO is empty and train_valid resolves train_pc equal to the held
fetch PC without recovery, the last queued producer has validated its
successor: release the saved full target as an architectural demand.
Require FIFO-empty as well as the PC match, so an earlier dynamic
instance of the same PC cannot authorize an unresolved younger one.
This must preserve symbolic progress, full address bits, and stale
prediction recovery. A resolved architectural demand is never silently
clamped, wrapped, or replaced with another instruction. Keep bus address
wired directly to the PC register and test boundary turnaround explicitly.

The explicit cost is a refill bubble after recovery and a missed
same-cycle full replacement. Four entries should absorb most bus
stalls and backend holds despite those costs. A 6% fitness gain at
unchanged Fmax requires about 4.16 million bracketed cycles; the
4.6% acceptance threshold requires fewer than 4.216 million. Measure
actual canonical stalled CoreMark cycles and median Gowin Fmax;
storage and head mux overhead can still erase the benefit. Do not
infer acceptance from the prior flow-through queue's cycle count.

The bounded prototype's placement options [0, 1, 2] measure
[61.323, 63.982, 63.982] MHz, with 4,236 LUT4, 1,164 FF, 76 LUT-RAM,
six BSRAMs and two DSPs. The unchanged CoreMark harness reports all
canonical CRCs, both timing markers, the required validation UART
literal, successful completion, and no OOB. Full RVFI ISS comparison
passes selftest and all three random programs with zero waits and
with both random bus stalls, plus a directed JAL at 0x000ffffc that
must turn around without speculative access to 0x00100000: ten runs
total. The probe is under cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/
registered4_frontier and leaves champion RTL unchanged. Reimplement
from this hypothesis and run all unchanged correctness/fitness gates;
full formal and directed FIFO/reset/stall validation remain required.

forwards, then chooses a PC or immediate before ALU computation.

lost to the flop-bank champion. Retain that winning storage and finish
registering the complete operand choices instead of changing storage.

Make each EX ALU operand a single masked-OR selection from registered
data, with its complete source choice registered at the ID/EX edge.
This is one operand-delivery timing optimization: remove late WB data
selection and serial forwarding-then-PC/immediate selection. Preserve

to mem_wb_t; on ordinary MEM capture assign

and sign/zero-extended load_data. WB w_data becomes a direct wire from
wb_data. Reset clears it; hold_wb retains it while valid clears exactly
as today. Preserve destination/write metadata and held-WB forwarding
eligibility. Existing alu_result/read_data fields can remain, but must
not recreate the late WB mux for any timed consumer.

Alongside existing three-bit raw-register forwarding selections,
register independent four-bit one-hot ALU source selections in core.
Bits 0,1,2 choose ID/EX base, next EX/MEM producer and next MEM/WB
producer; bit 3 chooses PC for A or immediate for B. Expose just
next_alu_a_pc and next_alu_b_imm from id_stage's exact ID/EX next-control
choice: reset or flush clears them; otherwise a hold uses current
registered is_auipc/alu_src, and an advance uses in.valid-qualified

as {next_alu_b_imm, next_fwd_rs2 & {3{!next_alu_b_imm}}}. Refresh every
edge, including holds, exactly as raw forwarding provenance does now.
Match actual producers entering or remaining in EX/MEM and MEM/WB;
do not substitute current-cycle destination tags.

fwd_ex_mem, fwd_mem_wb and in.pc. Form alu_b similarly from in.rs2_val,
fwd_ex_mem, fwd_mem_wb and in.imm. Each mask comes directly from its
registered selection bit. Remove the serial is_auipc/alu_src mux after
raw forwarding. Preserve the separate original raw rs1/rs2 forwarding
