title: Register predictor training at the execute advance boundary
motivation:
The champion achieves 70.604 MHz and fitness 160.12 at 4,409,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the
MEM/WB mem_to_reg control, passes through WB selection and EX operand
forwarding and branch comparison, and ends at a predictor counter
register in IF. The previous structural changes removed divider,
multiplier, forwarding-control and register-file timing bottlenecks.
Delaying branch recovery failed because it added a bubble per taken
transfer. Predictor table maintenance can instead be separated from
execution by a register without delaying architectural recovery.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert one registered predictor-training packet between EX resolution
and the existing tagged predictor's table update. Capture train_valid,
train_pc, train_eligible, train_jump, train_taken and train_target on
every edge in core.sv. Feed if_stage training exclusively from this
packet. Keep the existing combinational EX redirect and redirect_target
connection to IF and ID, the prediction lookup, all table dimensions,
tags, targets and two-bit counter policy unchanged. This is one
structural retiming of the predictor-maintenance path, not a change
to prediction capacity or algorithm and not an extra issue stage.

The packet valid bit records exactly the existing final EX advance:
in.valid && !stall && !reset && !execute_busy. It is assigned anew
each edge, including during memory and blocking-operation holds;
never retain a consumed valid packet when the pipeline stalls.
Capture a completed MUL/DIV/JALR instruction only on its final consume
edge, with the original pending PC and resolved target. Capture normal
instructions too, including ineligible and illegal resolutions, because
the predictor uses them to invalidate a matching stale prediction.
A packet generated before an imem/dmem stall still updates the table
once on the next edge. Reset clears packet validity and table validity,
cancelling any pending update. Preserve program order of consecutive
training packets; there is no queue or update backpressure.

Perform train_index, tag-hit checking, saturating counter update,
allocation and stale-entry invalidation inside IF from the registered
packet and the table state at application time. In particular, do not
register an old counter value or old tag hit alongside the packet:
consecutive resolutions to the same index must observe earlier updates,
and a stale nonbranch resolution must not invalidate an unrelated tag.
Do not add a combinational bypass from raw EX training to table writes
or fetch prediction. A one-cycle-later predictor update may change a
close re-fetch's speculative choice; existing prediction verification
and same-cycle architectural recovery must still correct it safely.

The desired timing cut is WB/EX branch resolution to training packet
flops, followed by packet flops to predictor table maintenance. It
removes counter read/modify/write and tag qualification from the live
execute operand cone without adding ordinary instruction latency.
The main risk is a competing ALU, redirect or table-read path limiting
Fmax, or extra prediction misses consuming the timing gain. At unchanged
cycles the 4.6 percent acceptance margin requires median Fmax above
approximately 73.852 MHz. The projected improvement is an estimate,
not a measured result; use actual stalled CoreMark cycles if they change.

forwarding, misalignment traps, exactly-once memory side effects and
contiguous RVFI retirement. Keep all existing checks and require

by bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle with the unchanged bus stalls.

title: Prequalify predictor recovery and pipeline resolved training events
motivation:
The champion reaches 160.12 iterations/sec at 70.604 MHz with 4,409,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the WB
mem_to_reg control, traverses operand forwarding and EX, and ends at
u_if's direction-counter storage: 20.173 ns across 37 cells. Predictor
training currently combines the late resolved branch outcome with a
tagged table lookup and saturating counter update in the same cycle.
Prior predicted-fetch queues saved cycles but lost to competing timing
cones, while delaying architectural branch recovery added costly bubbles.
Training is advisory state and can be delayed without delaying recovery,
instruction issue, memory effects, or architectural retirement. Recovery
currently also serializes branch comparison, target-misalignment trap
qualification, control selection, and prediction mismatch. Resolve the
static mismatch conditions before EX so the late branch outcome controls
a small selection, while a registered training event cuts counter updates.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming the existing predictor's recovery and maintenance is the single
architectural angle: keep its 32-entry full-tag bimodal prediction policy,
direct combinational fetch delivery, and immediate architectural recovery,
but prequalify recovery in decode and register resolved training events.
Do not add a fetch queue, prediction algorithm, or execution latency.

Add three bits to ID/EX: prediction_wrong_taken,
prediction_wrong_not_taken, and prediction_train_eligible. In ID, default
both mismatch bits to the fetch snapshot's prediction_selected. Set
prediction_train_eligible only for a decoder-legal conditional branch or
direct JAL whose existing direct_target is word aligned; JALR eligibility
waits for its registered actual target in EX. For an eligible branch,
prediction_wrong_taken is !prediction_selected OR
(direct_target != predicted_target), and prediction_wrong_not_taken is
prediction_selected. For an eligible direct JAL, both mismatch bits are
!prediction_selected OR (direct_target != predicted_target). Ordinary,
illegal, and misaligned direct transfers retain the default mismatch
bits, because their architectural successor is the existing fall-through.
Capture/hold/flush these bits exactly with the instruction and snapshot.
Keep the existing direct_target_match field compatible or allow its
unused physical logic to be pruned; no extra target adder is needed.

For a nonpending instruction in EX, select these two registered mismatch
bits with branch_cond. Both bits agree for nonbranches, so this selection
needs no extra late opcode, legality, or misalignment gating. For a
pending blocking instruction, recover using its captured prediction:
default to pending_prediction_q, and only for a captured legal jump use
!pending_prediction_q OR (pending_payload_q.branch_target !=
pending_predicted_target_q). JALR's registered actual target and launch
misalignment trap remain authoritative; MUL/DIV stale predictions still
recover only at completion. Keep train_valid's existing final-advance
gate and redirect = train_valid AND prediction_wrong. Keep redirect_target
and all architectural result/trap/RVFI calculations unchanged.

Use in.prediction_train_eligible for fast direct-transfer training.
When pending, eligibility is a captured legal jump with an aligned
pending branch_target. This removes the forwarded branch condition from
training eligibility: direct-target alignment and decoder legality are
already known in ID. Preserve the resolved train_taken, train_jump,
train_pc, and train_target values and once-per-final-advance semantics.

Insert one registered, in-order training-event stage inside if_stage
between the existing EX training outputs and the existing 32-entry
tagged bimodal BTB update. On every clock capture train_valid into an
event-valid flop; on a valid event capture its PC, eligibility, jump
classification, resolved outcome, and target. Apply the previous cycle's
event to the BTB on the next clock. Keep the existing fetch lookup,
predicted-PC selection, prediction snapshots, and immediate EX recovery
latency unchanged.

The event register accepts at most one final EX advance per cycle and
drains independently of frontend holds, current EX execute_busy, imem
readiness, and dmem readiness. Simultaneous application of an older event
and capture of a new event must sustain one event per clock. Capture
only the existing train_valid event, including completed blocking
instructions; never regenerate training from a held instruction. A
redirect must not cancel the event belonging to its resolving instruction
or the preceding event. Reset clears both BTB validity and event validity,
cancelling pre-reset pending training. Resetting unused payload flops is
optional because invalid events cannot read or update predictor state.

Compute the training index, tag hit, and counter update from the
registered event and the table state at application time. Preserve
legal/aligned eligibility, full tag and aligned full target, weak-taken
or weak-not-taken allocation on a miss, saturated conditional updates,
strongly-taken jump updates, and tag-qualified stale-entry invalidation.
In particular, do not carry an earlier counter value or train_hit into
the event register: consecutive updates to the same index must observe
all previous applications, and delayed invalidation must not erase an
unrelated replacement tag. Index/tag/target may be stored as their exact
existing bit slices instead of whole PCs, retaining alignment checks
before eligibility is recorded and all architecturally relevant bits.

Fetch sees only committed table contents. Do not bypass the pending EX
outcome or an updated counter into lookup, which would recreate the
branch-to-fetch combinational path. A branch revisited before its update
commits may receive the previous prediction; existing EX mismatch
recovery must correct it. Continue to carry the actual fetch prediction
unchanged through ID/EX and pending blocking-operation metadata. Preserve
immediate recovery for direction/target mismatches, stale hits on ordinary
instructions, changed JALR targets, and traps. Preserve existing held
operand refresh, load-use rules, exactly-once memory effects, full RVFI
operands/resolved successors/order, decoder legality, arithmetic and
ALTOPS behavior, nret=1, and every external port and evaluation contract.

The intended gain is Fmax from separating forwarded branch comparison
from serial recovery qualification, tag lookup, counter read-modify-write,
and BTB write qualification.
The explicit cost is one extra cycle of predictor-learning latency,
which can increase cold-start or very short-loop mispredictions without
imposing a pipeline bubble on every control transfer. At unchanged
cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above approximately 73.85 MHz.
An isolated prototype of this complete predictor retiming measures
vendor placement options [65.409, 75.432, 75.432] MHz, median 75.432 MHz,
with 5,374 LUT4, 2,126 FF, 44 LUT-RAM, four BSRAMs, and two DSPs. The
resulting frequency gain is 6.84 percent. Option 0's reported worst path
now runs from WB through EX/ALU to data memory, rather than predictor
storage or recovery. If cycles increase, scale the acceptance frequency
threshold by the measured cycle ratio. Competing ALU paths and final
implementation differences remain risks; measure canonical stalled
CoreMark cycles and median Gowin Fmax together. The scratch prototype is
under cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/prequalified_training1;
reimplement from this description because generated artifacts are
transient and are deleted before evaluation.

The combined prototype passes all six existing cocotb unit runners
(including all 40 pipeline cases, with only direct-EX metadata packing
adapted), all 53 unchanged fast formal checks, and full RVFI ISS cosim
of selftest plus all three random programs both with zero waits and
with random stalls. The unchanged canonical CoreMark harness validates
CRCs, required UART text, both timing markers, completion, and no OOB;
it reports exactly 4,409,538 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. A
fresh champion simulation reproduces that cycle count. Combined with
median vendor Fmax, this projects 171.07 iterations/sec, 6.84 percent
above 160.12, exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. These are
isolated prototype measurements, not an accepted tournament result;
rerun all gates on the final implementation.

Retain all existing checks. Add directed tests for back-to-back training
events, repeated-PC direction changes and saturation, index collisions,
stale-entry invalidation, and reset with an unapplied event. Exercise
capture/application across imem and dmem stalls, redirects, and blocking
operation completion; check no lost or duplicate update, retirement, or

assumes a same-edge table update, explicitly model the one-cycle training

Also test all six branch comparison kinds with taken/not-taken snapshot

direct EX stimulus. Retain its original captured-operand/completion and
trap assertions. Require unchanged unit, formal, stalled cosim,
CoreMark CRC/marker/UART, and vendor timing gates before acceptance.

title: Precompute direct-transfer recovery predicates during decode
motivation:
The champion scores 167.71 iterations/sec at 73.952 MHz with 4,409,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged Gowin placement-0 run
reproduces its 21.123 ns worst path: ID/EX operands, forwarding, branch
comparison, recovery qualification and high-fanout decode clear.
Prior micro_opt attempts addressed division, memory addresses, forwarding
and register-file delivery. Round 6's combined recovery prequalification
and delayed training reached 73.885 MHz on the older operand datapath;
delayed training alone regressed. The current champion already improves
final WB data and ALU source selection. Isolating static recovery
prequalification now targets the remaining EX control cone without
introducing the learning delay of those predictor attempts.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move only operand-independent direct-transfer recovery and training
qualifications across the existing ID/EX register. Keep the current
branch comparator, forwarding, predictor table, immediate EX recovery,
training-update timing and all instruction latencies. This is one
local control-logic retiming optimization, with no new execution stage
or predictor policy.

prediction_train_eligible bits to id_ex_t. In ID default both mismatch
bits to the actual fetch snapshot's prediction_selected. Define direct
eligibility as decoder-legal branch or direct JAL with word-aligned
direct_target; JALR waits for its existing registered actual target.
For an eligible branch set wrong_taken to !prediction_selected OR
(direct_target != predicted_target), retaining wrong_not_taken as
prediction_selected. For eligible direct JAL set both mismatch bits
to !prediction_selected OR (direct_target != predicted_target).
Ordinary/illegal instructions, JALR and misaligned direct targets
retain the defaults. Capture, reset, flush and hold these fields with

adder and prediction snapshot; add no lookup or wide datapath mux.

In EX, when no blocking payload is pending, select the two saved
mismatch bits directly with branch_cond. Both bits agree for
nonbranches, so this selection needs no following late opcode,
legality or misalignment qualification. Preserve branch_taken and
actual trap/RVFI successor calculations. A misaligned taken branch
still traps and falls through; an untaken branch with that target
remains legal, and stale predictions are corrected in both cases.

When a blocking payload is pending, default prediction_wrong to its
captured pending_prediction_q. Only a captured legal jump replaces it
with !pending_prediction_q OR (pending_payload_q.branch_target !=
pending_predicted_target_q). Use the authoritative registered JALR sum
and captured launch-time trap; MUL/DIV stale predictions still recover
only on final advance. Preserve train_valid and redirect's existing
final-advance gates and redirect_target.

For fast instructions drive train_eligible from the saved direct
eligibility bit. For pending completion, eligibility is a captured
legal jump with aligned registered branch_target. Preserve train_pc,
train_jump, train_taken and train_target and update the BTB on exactly
the current edge. Add no training-event register or delayed learning.
Eligibility no longer depends on branch_taken through ctrl_with_trap:
direct legality and alignment are already known in ID. Preserve
tag-qualified stale-entry invalidation and actual fetch snapshots.

Keep decoder defaults/validation, reset/flush/hold priorities, held
operand refresh, registered next-producer forwarding, pending-operation
capture/consumption, real and ALTOPS arithmetic, load-use bubbles, both
bus handshakes, traps, exactly-once side effects and nret=1 ports intact.
The intended gain is less serial control logic after forwarded branch

title: Isolate execute between registered operands and registered recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 167.71 iterations/sec at 73.952 MHz with 4,409,538
bracketed cycles. Its worst path spans EX, IF and core control. Structural
r4s1 registered forwarding provenance, r5s1 preserved operand flops and
r6s0 registered final WB data, but EX still combines late data selection,
computation and frontend recovery. Earlier recovery retiming failed
before prediction existed because every taken transfer paid another
bubble. Today correct prediction can avoid that fee. Local probes find
that recovery retiming alone exposes the forwarded ALU path at 69.874
MHz, while actual operand retiming alone exposes EX-to-frontend-to-operand
capture at 65.451 MHz. Both register boundaries are necessary to isolate
the same execution stage from its incoming bypass and outgoing recovery
feedback; neither partial boundary is the proposed final architecture.

bracketed cycles. Its worst path spans EX, IF and core control. Structural

computation and frontend recovery. Earlier recovery retiming failed

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make EX a computation stage bounded by complete operand registers on
entry and complete resolution registers on exit. This is one structural
change to the placement of execution boundaries, retaining the existing
single-issue pipeline, tagged predictor policy, arithmetic units, bus
contract, regfile and nret=1. Ordinary arithmetic and correctly predicted
transfers retain issue throughput; only actual prediction recovery gains
one cycle and squashes one more younger position. Do not add a general
execution bubble or combine this with caches or prediction-policy changes.

Before the existing ID/EX edge, use forward_unit's next-producer matching
to select actual next-state data, rather than registering only selections.
EX exposes effective next EX/MEM alu_result beside next_rd/next_w_en;
MEM exposes its effective next final WB value, selecting accepted load
data or ALU result identically to MEM/WB and retaining WB data on holds.
Match the decoded source addresses to these producers with EX priority
over MEM/WB and nonzero destination checks. Base data is the regfile's
write-first read. During holds use held source addresses and held raw
base operands, preserving values as old producers drain. Keep load-use
bubbling and older data-memory hold priority: never capture a load's
address as its data or capture unavailable bus data.

Add alu_a_val and alu_b_val to id_ex_t. Capture resolved raw rs1/rs2,
ALU-a selected between AUIPC PC and resolved rs1, and ALU-b selected
between the decoded immediate and resolved rs2. On a hold refresh raw
operands against the effective next producers and rebuild ALU operands
from the held instruction's control, PC and immediate. Reset/flush has
the existing priority and clears validity and operand state. EX consumes
raw operand and complete ALU operand flops directly, removing its data
forwarding/PC/immediate muxes and obsolete source-selection registers.
Branch, store and RVFI use raw values; arithmetic uses complete operands.
Blocking operations capture these resolved operands once at launch and
expose completed results to the new capture mux at the consume edge.

At EX's output boundary, register prediction_wrong and exact training
metadata alongside the EX/MEM instruction on every final EX advance.
Reuse its PC, resolved pc_next, branch and target fields where exact;
a parallel registered control record held with EX/MEM is also acceptable.
For completed MUL/DIV/JALR use original captured pending metadata and
prediction snapshots. The record includes ordinary/illegal instructions
so stale predictions are recovered and tag-qualified invalidation occurs.
No live EX comparison or target may drive fetch, decode recovery, or BTB
writes. Drive redirect and training only from accepted registered MEM
state: mem_accept = EX/MEM.valid && !stall_ex_mem && !reset;
redirect = mem_accept && recovery_needed; target = registered pc_next.
Correct prediction causes no new squash, stall or redirect.

Registered recovery squashes both younger ID/EX and current EX positions,
while the resolving MEM instruction proceeds into MEM/WB and older WB
retirement remains intact. Add explicit EX squash, dominant over younger
execute-busy/load-use holds. Suppress younger launch and consume, clear
younger pending validity, emit a fully zeroed EX/MEM bubble, and describe
that bubble in next producer data/metadata. Its valid, mem_read,
mem_write and reg_write are all zero. Flush ID/EX and its operand state
on the same recovery edge. In-order launch rules must prevent younger
slow work starting behind a held resolving MEM request; verify no orphan
multiplier/divider remains busy. Reset cancels every pending unit/record.

Preserve an unaccepted older MEM transaction and its record; it emits
neither recovery nor training until acceptance. A nonmemory branch/jump
in MEM must not wait for unrelated low dmemReady. Recovery overrides
instruction-bus holds and younger blocking operations. Apply predictor
training exactly once per accepted MEM record, including the resolving
record on its redirect edge. Squashed younger instructions must not
train. Read current table tags/counters at application, preserving ordered
saturated updates and tag-qualified invalidation. Keep actual prediction
snapshots and the existing policy. Illegal/misaligned/stale predictions
recover to the instruction's existing actual successor; preserve traps
and suppression of link writes. Do not use an unregistered training or
recovery bypass that recreates the EX feedback loop.

Keep next-producer controls tied to effective next state, including held
requests, pending completion, alignment traps and squash bubbles. Preserve
retained-WB forwarding eligibility independently of retirement valid.
Keep the flop-bank regfile and real operand flops; do not use timing
exceptions or synthesis-only behavior. All top-level ports, nret=1,
decoder default-illegal rules, RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic, memory
handshakes, exactly-once side effects, complete RVFI values/successors
and contiguous order remain mandatory. Arithmetic-to-operand-capture
bypass remains a competing path, so vendor timing must verify the gain.

The isolated combined prototype is under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/isolated_execute. Reimplement
from this description because generated artifacts are transient. The
operand-boundary component passes all 43 existing pipeline cases, all
53 unchanged fast formal checks, and selftest plus three random full
RVFI instruction cosims each with and without random bus stalls; its
stalled CoreMark preserves 4,409,538 cycles and canonical CRCs. The
registered-resolution component also validates CoreMark and all eight
instruction cosims, with 4,483,027 bracketed cycles. These component
checks do not prove the combined implementation. The complete circuit
must rerun unchanged gates. With that approximately 1.67% recovery cost,
acceptance requires median Fmax above roughly 78.64 MHz; 85 MHz would
imply about 13% fitness gain. Expected improvement remains a projection
until combined median vendor timing and canonical cycles are measured.

Add directed tests for actual same-edge EX and accepted-load capture,
held operands, source conflicts, x0/WB bypass, all branch comparisons,
AUIPC/immediate operands, completion consumers, predicted hits, direction
and target misses, stale/illegal/misaligned entries, long dmem waits,
irrelevant readiness lows, imem stalls, adjacent resolution records,
reset and younger store/branch/MUL/DIV/JALR squash. Assert exact operands,
results, successor PCs, traps, retirement order and memory/training
effects. Adapt direct EX packing to 328-bit ID/EX and registered recovery
timing without weakening assertions. Evaluate unchanged median Gowin
Fmax times canonical marker-bracketed iterations/cycle before acceptance.

title: Parallel BTB banks with local hysteresis and prequalified recovery
motivation: The champion scores 167.71 at 73.952 MHz with 4,409,538 timed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path crosses EX, IF and decode across 42 cells. The BTB uses dynamically indexed tags, targets and counters, serializing a table read before the tag comparison and feeding training through a selected counter read-modify-write. The prior registered-training proposal only moved the competing limit: an isolated rerun with decode-prequalified recovery on the latest champion reaches 72.840 MHz with unchanged cycles. Instead, represent the same predictor as independent flop entries, analogous to the separately generated flop-bank register file that improved round five, with parallel full-tag comparison and local two-bit state updates. This changes predictor hardware organization while retaining the proven prediction policy and learning latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the existing 32-entry fully tagged bimodal BTB as 32 separately generated constant-index flop banks, with parallel tag comparison and balanced masked-OR target selection. The single angle is removing selected table-read and counter-update muxes from the predictor control cone. Keep the current prediction policy, direct combinational instruction delivery, immediate EX recovery, arithmetic latency and original once-per-EX-advance training latency. Do not add a FIFO, delayed training stage or another predictor algorithm.

Each bank contains a resettable valid bit, full 25-bit PC[31:7] tag, aligned 30-bit target[31:2], and two direction-state flops. Decode fetch PC[6:2] against that bank's constant index in parallel with comparing its local tag to PC[31:7]. Its selected signal is fetch-row AND valid AND tag-match AND direction. Mask the bank's full aligned target by this selected signal. Combine all 32 masked targets and all selected bits through explicit five-level binary OR trees, like the existing register-file read tree. Select the reduced target when any selected bit is set, otherwise PC+4. Distinct row selects guarantee at most one selected entry. Do not truncate high PC bits or use a partial tag. Store each word in a separate generated local register, so synthesis does not reconstruct dynamically indexed LUT-RAM read ports before tag comparison.

Encode the saturating counter as direction D and strength S: strongly not taken=(0,1), weakly not taken=(0,0), weakly taken=(1,0), strongly taken=(1,1). On a matching conditional update with actual outcome T, assign D_next = S ? D : T and S_next = (D == T), using both OLD state bits. These equations implement exactly the existing two-bit saturation, including weak-state crossing and both bounds, without an adder, saturation comparator or dynamically selected old counter. title: Remove redundant validity masks before execute capture
motivation:
The champion reaches 187.23 iterations/sec at 83.934 MHz and 4,483,027
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its complete ID/EX operands and registered
recovery have removed the older forwarding/frontend feedback cone.
The reproduced Gowin worst path crosses fast ALU result selection and
execute payload/capture logic before the data-memory address port.

then zeros it again with fast_emit, which already requires in.valid.
Destination matching also sees validity-masked payload tags. These
repeated masks add control fanout and obscure the final capture mux.
Prior micro_opt validity work targeted fetch/decode before prediction
and operand retiming; this targets the current EX capture boundary.

title: Separate registered load/store requests from scalar execution
motivation:
The champion reaches median 83.934 MHz and 187.23 iterations/sec with
4,483,027 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its option-0 critical path is
18.864 ns from a complete ID/EX operand to a data-memory address input.
The fresh vendor report shows only two cells inside the ALU followed
by eight cells in general result selection and EX state selection.
Thus the memory interface still inherits arbitrary scalar ALU,
jump-link and blocking-completion selection even though a load/store
address needs only rs1 plus its immediate. The r3s0 address experiment
improved timing before losing to the stronger registered MUL/JALR
change; its remaining scalar path has since been cut by r4-r7. A
separate registered memory-request lane is now a plausible way to
remove this measured coupling without increasing instruction cycles.

title: Two-entry fixed-head predicted fetch queue preserves operand timing
motivation: The champion scores 187.23 iterations/sec at 83.934 MHz and 4,483,027 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The existing 32-entry tagged BTB already handles most transfer bubbles, but fetch loses ready bus opportunities during load-use, data-memory and blocking-execute holds. Prior queues saved cycles while exposing frontend or operand-delivery timing. Complete execution operands and MEM recovery are now registered. A small queue with a constant flop head can overlap predicted fetch with these holds without an indexed queue read or live instruction bypass feeding decode. Exploratory four-entry circular and flow-through probes saved 7.82% of cycles but reached only 62.122 and 70.220 MHz; a four-entry registered fixed head saved 5.99% but reached 78.500 MHz. Reduce the same predictor lookahead mechanism to two entries to limit area and routing pressure while preserving its timing boundaries.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one two-entry registered queue of complete predicted-fetch snapshots inside if_stage. This is a single predicted-fetch lookahead change: use the existing BTB to accept bus words during backend holds and supply buffered words during instruction stalls. Keep BTB size, full tags and targets, counter policy, MEM-accepted training and recovery, complete operand capture, producer forwarding and all arithmetic latencies unchanged.

Use two separately generated constant-index flop words, with the oldest snapshot always in entry zero and the second in entry one. Store full PC, instruction, prediction_selected, full predicted_target and a one-bit frontier marker. Do not use dynamically indexed storage or read pointers and do not bypass a live bus instruction into decode. Only the previously registered fixed head feeds instruction, PC and prediction payloads. Occupancy controls head validity separately from these data bits. ID reads live register values on consumption. Each accepted bus word enters the queue once; PCs are stored directly, never reconstructed from consumed predictions.

Maintain occupancy from zero to two. Accept a bus word only with imemReady, capacity at cycle start and no reset, recovery or frontier wait. Ordinary fetch-PC enable depends on registered capacity and bus readiness, never a backend pop. Deliberately refuse same-cycle replacement of a full queue. Advance fetch PC using the prediction for the accepted word only. Pop only a valid registered head that ID can consume without load-use, genuine older dmem wait or execute_busy. On pop shift entry one to entry zero. Append an accepted bus snapshot at old occupancy minus pop, giving append priority over shift for that destination. Use constant-index per-word write enables comparing occupancy minus pop with the bank index. Push alone increments count, pop alone decrements count and simultaneous push/pop preserves count. Invalid words need no payload reset; reset clears occupancy. An empty queue produces an ID bubble and an accepted bus word becomes available on the following cycle. Accept the deliberate refill cycle to keep queue availability out of register-address and operand-data selection.

Handle raw imemReady locally in IF. Remove it from the hazard unit's backend-consumption hold; load-use detection inspects the presented head and its availability. Keep raw head payload independent of redirect. The existing ID flush cancels younger capture and overrides holds; gate pop, push and head validity on accepted recovery. Preserve EX/MEM genuine memory waits, retained MEM/WB forwarding data, held operand refresh and pending-operation cancellation. Do not add queue controls to registered operand outputs, ALU data or registered resolution.

A MEM-accepted redirect overrides every hold, clears queue occupancy, discards same-edge fetch acceptance and installs the full resolved target. Correct predictions preserve queued work. Train on the existing once-per-MEM-acceptance event, including its redirect edge, never on queue activity or squashed work. Carry each snapshot's original prediction through ID and blocking-operation capture. Preserve recovery for direction and target disagreement, stale ordinary or illegal predictions and misaligned transfers.

Bound speculative runahead at the executable-memory frontier. When an accepted word predicts a successor outside [0, 0x00100000), save the full successor, mark that exact snapshot, and hold physical fetch PC at its accepted address. While waiting accept no duplicate bus word; queued work drains. Carry the marker through ID/EX, EX/MEM and pending-operation payloads. The existing train_valid MEM acceptance carrying the marker validates that exact dynamic instruction. If no recovery is required, release the saved full successor as architectural demand. Recovery and reset cancel the wait; an older recovery squashes its marked younger instruction. Only one marker can be outstanding. Do not authorize release by PC equality, truncate high address bits, clamp a true architectural demand or block symbolic forward progress.

Keep nret=1, all top-level ports, full PC/target/address widths, validated default-illegal decoding, actual RVFI operands and successors, monotonic contiguous retirement order, exactly-once stores, real and ALTOPS arithmetic and all unchanged evaluation gates. Use packed vector wires for inter-bank snapshot connections and whole-word flop writes for formal frontend compatibility. The added frontier bit changes ID/EX to 329 bits and EX/MEM to 296 bits; update every explicit packed mask and test layout consistently.

Measure canonical bracketed CoreMark cycles and median vendor Fmax together. Four-entry measurements establish stall-overlap potential, not acceptance of this two-entry proposal. Small fixed-head storage is intended to retain about 5-6% cycle savings while keeping median Fmax near the champion. Reimplement and rerun unchanged correctness and fitness gates; scratch artifacts are transient and deleted before evaluation. Preserve exact architectural test assertions. For tests that change imem contents, schedule replacement before the affected word's bus acceptance or explicitly check the saved accepted snapshot; replacement must not retroactively rewrite queued instructions. Update cycle expectations only for the declared registered refill behavior, retaining exact instructions, operands, traps, successors, order and side effects.

title: Predecode and fuse fast execute result selection
motivation:
The champion scores 187.23 at 83.934 MHz with 4,483,027 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at an ID/EX operand
and crosses the fast ALU and execute result capture. The r8s0
micro_opt removed redundant input-valid masking but improved fitness
by only 4.45 percent, below the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.
The remaining fast result still traverses an operation case mux,
a jump-link mux, and emission selection. Earlier operand retiming
demonstrates that moving selector work before a register boundary
can improve timing without changing instruction cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predecode fast result choices into ID/EX and fuse operation, jump-link,
and fast-emission selection into one parallel masked-OR result bank
at the existing EX/MEM capture boundary. This is a local execute
selection optimization: preserve every pipeline boundary, instruction
latency, predictor policy, memory handshake, and nret=1 interface.

Add a 12-bit ID/EX fast_result_sel field. Bits 0 through 10 correspond
exactly to ALU_ADD through ALU_LUI; bit 11 selects the PC+4 jump link.
Decode it in ID as dec_is_jump ? 12'h800 :
dec_alu_op <= ALU_LUI ? (12'b1 << dec_alu_op) : 12'b0.
Capture, hold, reset, and flush it with that same instruction.
Both JAL and JALR select only the link choice. Compute JALR's target
independently from the ADD candidate, clearing bit zero as before;
do not use the link-selected ALU output to generate its target.
Preserve its existing registered pending completion and PC+4 link.
MUL and DIV continue to use their unchanged clocked units and held
completion interface. Illegal operations must retain trap behavior
and cannot become register or memory producers.

Expose independent combinational RV32I candidate results from ALU
operands and use the registered one-hot choices instead of decoding
the binary ALU operation after ID/EX. Preserve modulo-32 arithmetic,
signed and unsigned comparison semantics, five-bit shift amounts,
and sign extension for SRA. Keep the original binary operation for
the multiplier/divider interfaces and any compatible standalone ALU
output; an adapter must not restore a binary case mux on core's
fast operand-to-result path.

Define the un-emitted arithmetic result as the OR of candidates
0 through 10 masked by their registered choice bits. The pending
launch payload's result is this word OR PC+4 masked by choice bit 11;
MUL/DIV later overwrite that result with their held unit completion.

title: Immutable operand capture removes stall-dependent bypass topology
motivation:
Complete ID/EX operand registers and registered recovery raised fitness
to 187.23, but retained the earlier forwarding-provenance design's held
operand repair network. The last structural attempt preserved CoreMark
cycles while regressing to 82.509 MHz; its critical path runs from the
ID/EX destination through EX producer control and forwarding back into
ID/EX operands. The recent 87.672 MHz validity-mask simplification also
exposes a hazard-to-operand capture path and misses the 4.6% acceptance
margin. Operand words are already fully resolved before acceptance, so
treating accepted operands as immutable can remove this whole control
topology rather than merely relocate the memory adder.

hypothesis.motivation:
Complete ID/EX operand registers and registered recovery raised fitness
to 187.23, but retained the earlier forwarding-provenance design's held
operand repair network. The last structural attempt preserved CoreMark
cycles while regressing to 82.509 MHz; its critical path runs from the
ID/EX destination through EX producer control and forwarding back into
ID/EX operands. The recent 87.672 MHz validity-mask simplification also
exposes a hazard-to-operand capture path and misses the 4.6% acceptance
margin. Operand words are already fully resolved before acceptance, so

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the ID/EX boundary as an instruction record with immutable,
fully resolved raw and ALU operands. Capture all operand words together
only when decode actually accepts an instruction. A held instruction
preserves every operand bit; remove the second held-source forwarding
instance and held-operand rebuilding. Keep reset and accepted recovery
flush dominant over the hold. Do not add pipeline stages, instruction
bubbles, speculative memory access, or changes to prediction policy.

Establish the capture invariant explicitly: every nonzero source of an
accepted instruction equals the youngest preceding legal register
writer's final result. A producer in EX bypasses its fast arithmetic,
jump link, or completed blocking result. A load in EX forces the existing
load-use bubble; a load in MEM bypasses only on bus acceptance. An older
genuine MEM wait prevents decode acceptance. A pending blocking EX
instruction prevents decode acceptance until completion can advance;
its completion edge must bypass its exact captured destination/result.
Otherwise use the accepted MEM final load/ALU value, then the register
file's existing write-first value. Preserve youngest-writer priority,
nonzero destination checks and alignment-trap write suppression. Check
the invariant under long stalls and simultaneous writes before removing
repair; an unavailable value must prevent acceptance, never be guessed.

Use this acceptance invariant to specialize normal decode forwarding.
It needs only the concrete EX fast, EX link, EX completed and accepted
MEM candidates plus the write-first register-file base. Remove held
EX/MEM and retained MEM/WB candidates from this capture network. Their
values are either already in an immutable held operand or unavailable
during a decode hold; physical WB writes continue to use valid normally.
Factor genuine memory hold, reset and recovery controls into the operand
bank's capture enable/clear instead of every 32-bit candidate mask.
For candidate selection use source-specific operation/validity and
completion qualification, with fast/link versus pending completion
mutually exclusive. Pending completion readiness still controls the
acceptance decision. Never use a stale completion or a load address
as data. Preserve existing EX/MEM advance and request/consume signals;
new decode candidate eligibility is separate from side-effect emission.

Build ALU-a from resolved rs1 or AUIPC PC and ALU-b from resolved rs2 or
the decoded immediate, without a stall-dependent held/new masked OR.
Write raw operands, complete ALU operands and instruction metadata on
the same accepted edge; retain them together otherwise. Keep genuine
operand flops and the existing flop-bank register file. EX and blocking
unit launch consume these immutable words directly. This single change
removes held repair and acceptance controls from operand data selection
while retaining ordinary execution and recovery latency.

Keep nret=1 and all ports, full addresses and PC widths, default-illegal
decoding, exact RV32M and ALTOPS results, accepted MEM predictor training,
exactly-once memory effects and contiguous RVFI retirement. RVFI must
report the original accepted operand values. Validate unchanged unit,
formal and instruction cosim gates and canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs,
UART literal and marker-bracketed cycles. Judge median vendor Fmax times
actual iterations/cycle; unchanged cycles require more than 87.795 MHz
for acceptance. An estimated 92 MHz would improve fitness about 10%.
Competing arithmetic and predictor paths may limit the gain.

title: Three-slot predicted fetch queue with local occupancy control
motivation:
The two-entry fixed-head predicted fetch queue reached 195.67 iterations/sec,
a 4.51 percent gain that narrowly missed the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
A three-entry prototype saves 5.13 percent of canonical CoreMark cycles,
but binary occupancy and subtract-to-select append control reached only
78.578 MHz. Preserve the additional predicted lookahead while replacing
global occupancy arithmetic with local occupied bits and constant-bank
append enables. Execution, forwarding and the existing BTB policy stay
unchanged; this is one predictor-front-end architectural change.

hypothesis.motivation:
The two-entry fixed-head predicted fetch queue reached 195.67 iterations/sec,
a 4.51 percent gain that narrowly missed the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
A three-entry prototype saves 5.13 percent of canonical CoreMark cycles,
but binary occupancy and subtract-to-select append control reached only
78.578 MHz. Preserve the additional predicted lookahead while replacing

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add three registered complete predicted-fetch snapshots inside if_stage.
Keep the existing 32-entry fully tagged bimodal BTB, full targets, exact
counter policy and once-per-MEM-acceptance training latency. Accept bus
words during backend holds and deliver saved words during imem stalls.
Use separately generated constant-index flop words, with entry zero
always the oldest snapshot and the sole source of decode data. Store full
PC, instruction, prediction_selected, full predicted_target and a frontier
marker. Use packed-vector inter-bank connections and whole-word writes
for formal compatibility. Never bypass live instruction data into decode
or reconstruct queued PCs. Resolve operands when ID actually consumes.

Replace binary count/pointers with registered prefix occupancy v0,v1,v2:
empty=000, one=001, two=011, full=111. Reset/recovery clear the bits.
pop = v0 AND backend-ready AND not reset/recovery.
push = imemReady AND !v2 AND !frontier-wait AND not reset/recovery.
Refuse same-cycle replacement of an initially full queue, keeping push
and ordinary fetch-PC advancement independent of pop/backend-ready.
Derive the following constant-bank append enables from OLD state:
append0 = push AND (!v0 OR (pop AND !v1));
append1 = push AND ((v0 AND !v1 AND !pop) OR (v1 AND !v2 AND pop));
append2 = push AND v1 AND !pop.
Append has priority over shift for its bank. Otherwise pop shifts bank
one into zero and bank two into one. Bank two holds unless appended.
Invalid payloads need no reset. Update occupancy using OLD state:
v0_next = push OR (v0 AND !pop) OR v1;
v1_next = (v1 AND !pop) OR v2 OR (push AND v0 AND (!pop OR v1));
v2_next = (v2 AND !pop) OR (push AND v1 AND !pop).
This preserves the three-entry prototype's schedule while removing
decrement-to-append logic and indexed queue reads. Test all transitions.

Handle raw imemReady locally in IF. Backend consumption uses head
availability, head source fields, load-use, genuine older dmem hold and
execute_busy; raw bus readiness must not hold an available head. Keep
payload bits independent of redirect and qualify validity separately.
ID flush overrides holds. MEM-accepted recovery cancels push/pop, clears
occupancy and installs the full resolved target regardless of fetch or
backend holds. Correct predictions retain buffered work. Advance fetch
PC only on actual push and keep each accepted word's exact prediction
snapshot through ID and pending operations. Learn only on the existing
once-per-MEM-acceptance event, including its own redirect edge; queue
activity and squashed work cannot train independently.

Bound speculation at the executable-memory frontier. If a pushed word's
predicted successor is outside [0,0x00100000), mark that exact dynamic
snapshot, save its full successor and hold physical fetch PC at its
accepted address. While waiting accept no duplicates; queued work drains.
Carry the marker through ID/EX, EX/MEM and pending payloads. Its exact
MEM-accepted event authorizes release of the saved full successor as
architectural demand when no recovery is required. Recovery/reset cancel
the wait. Never release by PC equality, truncate high bits, clamp actual
demand or block symbolic forward progress. Only one marker is outstanding.

Preserve nret=1, external IO, full PCs/targets, default-illegal validated
decoding, all traps, actual RVFI operands/successors, contiguous order,
held operand refresh, load-use/bus semantics, exactly-once stores and
real/ALTOPS arithmetic. The marker makes IF/ID 99, ID/EX 329 and EX/MEM
296 bits; update packed masks/test layouts consistently. Use numeric or
frontend-supported mask widths: Yosys rejects $bits(type) inside the
exploratory replicated-mask expression. Change no evaluation contracts.

The binary-control three-entry prototype passes full RVFI ISS cosim for
selftest and all three random programs, both zero-wait and stalled. Its
canonical CoreMark run validates every CRC, UART success text, timing
markers, completion and no OOB, taking 4,252,977 bracketed cycles versus
the freshly reproduced champion's 4,483,027. These establish the lookahead
opportunity, not final acceptance. At that schedule median Gowin Fmax
must exceed approximately 83.25 MHz to beat 187.23 by more than 4.6
percent. Rerun all gates on the final local-occupancy version; a competing
operand-forwarding timing path is the main risk. Prototype sources under
cores/bench/generated/hypothesis_probe/queue3_valids are transient and
must be reimplemented because generated artifacts are removed before eval.

Retain all existing architectural assertions. Registered refill adds one
cycle after recovery. Mutation tests must change a word before its bus
acceptance or explicitly verify the previously accepted snapshot before
the replacement. Internal checks must use the presented queue head,
rather than assuming io_imemAddr is decode PC. Adapt only declared
refill timing and fetch-position assumptions while keeping exact PC
sequences, operands, traps, successors, retirement order and side effects.

title: Use conditional EX/MEM capture instead of wide emission masks
motivation: The champion scores 187.23 at 83.934 MHz with 4,483,027 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged placement-1 run reproduced 83.934 MHz and found tightly competing EX/ALU-to-ID operand paths and branch-to-pending-payload paths. The r8s0 experiment removed EX's redundant input-valid mask and gained 4.45%, just below the 4.6% acceptance margin. EX/MEM still forms every one of its 295 payload bits through a held/completed/fast masked OR with an implicit all-zero bubble. This makes late emission controls part of the result capture datapath even when only validity and control fields need a bubble encoding.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 187.23 at 83.934 MHz with 4,483,027 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged placement-1 run reproduced 83.934 MHz and found tightly competing EX/ALU-to-ID operand paths and branch-to-pending-payload paths. The r8s0 experiment removed EX's redundant input-valid mask and gained 4.45%, just below the 4.6% acceptance margin. EX/MEM still forms every one of its 295 payload bits through a held/completed/fast masked OR with an implicit all-zero bubble. This makes late emission controls part of the result capture datapath even when only validity and control fields need a bubble encoding.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize EX/MEM payload storage as one local capture-control change. Replace the 295-bit emission-masked OR feeding the physical EX/MEM register with conditional capture of concrete payloads. Preserve the existing instruction latency, pipeline topology, forwarding, predictor policy, blocking units and nret=1 contract.

Keep full synchronous reset clearing. A genuine older MEM stall holds the entire EX/MEM record, with the same priority as the existing held_emit term. When not stalled, accepted older recovery clears the entire EX/MEM record to zero. Otherwise capture completed_payload on completed_emit, capture payload on fast_emit, and on an ordinary non-emitting cycle clear only reg_q.valid and reg_q.ctrl, retaining the other data fields. No stale mem_read, mem_write or reg_write bit may survive a bubble. Reset, stall, recovery, completion and fast advancement must retain the original source priorities; an asserted stall and squash must still retain the older held record while canceling younger pending work. Recovery metadata must retain its current update semantics and cannot become live on an invalid record.

Remove the separate in.valid mask around construction of the combinational fast/launch payload, as r8s0 did. Launch and fast_emit already require valid input. Keep every payload field correct for an emitted instruction and keep the existing source-specific producer eligibility, link selection, alignment traps and pending capture. Keep the effective next-state summary used by forwarding logically identical to the old fully zeroed reg_d expression: it is a producer description, not necessarily a literal copy of the retained invalid physical register. Producer write eligibility must continue to require validity or an actual emission; a bubble's retained rd/result must never suppress another forwarding source.

The intended timing gain comes from replacing wide data masking and implicit zero selection with a payload capture enable, combined with removing redundant input-valid masking. Ordinary invalid data is unobservable, while explicit zero control fields preserve the existing MEM/WB held-producer discipline. Do not change ID's bubble representation, reset or flush logic. Do not remove the held-operand repair network or register-file flops. This remains one EX capture micro_opt, with no extra execution cycle, new memory structure or changed predictor.

Audit every consumer of the retained invalid EX/MEM payload: memory read/write enables, dmem hold detection, accepted MEM producer qualification, predictor training and recovery, retirement, and retained MEM/WB forwarding. All must retain their existing validity qualifications. On an ordinary bubble MEM/WB may capture stale data but must capture zero register-write control, so a later data-memory hold cannot expose a ghost WB producer. Preserve bounded accesses, exactly-once stores, strict RVFI order, original retiring operands and PCs, legality and alignment traps, and both real and ALTOPS RV32M arithmetic.

Require the unchanged unit, fast formal and stalled instruction cosim gates and canonical marker-bracketed CoreMark CRC/UART checks. Add directed coverage for a useful fast result followed by imem bubbles, long pending MUL/DIV/JALR sequences, same-destination consumers, memory holds, wrong-path memory operations and blocking launches, reset, and accepted recovery. Check no false producer, duplicate retirement, predictor training or memory effect from retained invalid payload. Preserve existing reset and recovery zero-bubble assertions; tests of ordinary invalid payload may inspect validity/control and externally observable behavior without requiring unused data bits to be zero.

Estimate six percent higher fitness, with low confidence: capture-enable feedback, mapping choices and competing decode/predictor paths can limit the gain. CoreMark cycles should remain unchanged. Acceptance then requires median vendor Fmax above 87.795 MHz. Preliminary isolated arithmetic, operand-delivery and control probes did not exceed that threshold, so no accepted improvement is claimed. The implementation phase must judge median Gowin Fmax multiplied by measured iterations/cycle; the hypothesis must not be accepted on resource reduction or RVFI pruning alone.

Exercise nonzero records followed by ordinary bubbles, blocking launches/completion, genuine older MEM holds, simultaneous stall/squash, reset and accepted recovery. Check retained invalid EX/MEM payload cannot cause a ghost producer, memory transaction, predictor update or retirement through imem stalls, memory waits, pending MUL/DIV/JALR, dependent consumers and recovery. Preserve exact RVFI results/operands/order, exactly-once stores and every hard-invariant check.

Preserve exact RVFI results/operands/order, exactly-once stores and every hard-invariant check.

title: Separate decoded instruction storage from operand capture with early bypass matching
motivation:
The champion scores 187.23 at 83.934 MHz and 4,483,027 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural r8s1 moved memory request formation but
exposed an ID/EX destination-to-forwarding-to-operand path and lost
1.70 percent. Structural r9s1 removed held operand repair but exposed
instruction-bus-to-decoder-to-immediate-to-target-match timing and
lost 2.13 percent. These competing paths need a new register boundary,
rather than another simplification of the existing capture mux.
r4s1 demonstrated that registering bypass provenance improves timing;
r7s1 demonstrated the value of complete EX operand flops. A separate
decoded-instruction/operand-read boundary can retain both benefits.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 187.23 at 83.934 MHz and 4,483,027 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural r8s1 moved memory request formation but
exposed an ID/EX destination-to-forwarding-to-operand path and lost
1.70 percent. Structural r9s1 removed held operand repair but exposed
instruction-bus-to-decoder-to-immediate-to-target-match timing and
lost 2.13 percent. These competing paths need a new register boundary,
rather than another simplification of the existing capture mux.
r4s1 demonstrated that registering bypass provenance improves timing;
r7s1 demonstrated the value of complete EX operand flops. A separate
decoded-instruction/operand-read boundary can retain both benefits.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the current combined decode and operand-capture stage into a
registered decoded-instruction stage followed by an operand-read
stage. Preserve single issue and nret=1. The new decoded record stores
the validated control word, expanded immediate, PC, instruction,
source/destination addresses and original prediction snapshot.
Operand-read resolves raw source words and selects complete ALU
operands into the existing ID/EX operand flops. EX continues to consume
only complete registered operands; do not move its ALU behind a live
forwarding mux. This is one pipeline-boundary change, not a fetch FIFO
or a predictor-policy change. Consecutive ready independent instructions
must still issue and retire at one per cycle after pipeline fill.

Register source-to-producer tag matches at the new decoded boundary,
before the cycle that carries bypass result words. Match an incoming
decoded instruction against the instruction advancing from operand-read
to EX and the instruction advancing from EX to MEM. These become the
youngest EX and accepted-MEM candidates in its operand-read cycle.
Derive these predicted positions from actual stage transfer/hold/bubble
priorities, not an assumed unconditional shift. Keep individual match
bits for both ages, so final write suppression can fall back to the
next older writer. Late data availability, memory acceptance, completion
and trap qualification gate registered matches; they must not require
live five-bit destination comparisons before operand-word capture.
Give a qualifying younger writer priority over the older candidate and
the existing write-first register-file base; x0 always selects zero.

During an operand-read hold, rebase the small registered provenance

title: Three-entry predicted fetch stream with empty-queue direct delivery
motivation:
The registered-head two-entry predictor queue reached a 4.51 percent gain,
just below the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. The three-entry version reduced
CoreMark cycles by 5.13 percent but reached only 81.598 MHz. Registered-only
delivery adds a refill cycle whenever recovery empties the queue. A direct
empty-queue path can remove that penalty while keeping lookahead during
backend holds. A three-entry flow-through prototype validates canonical
CoreMark in 4,146,458 bracketed cycles versus a freshly reproduced champion's
4,483,027, a 7.51 percent cycle reduction. Four entries save only another
13,951 cycles and reduce median Fmax to 78.475 MHz. Choose three entries to
retain nearly all measured cycle savings with fewer payload flops and less
queue control/routing. The angle is the predicted fetch stream's refill
and stall-overlap schedule; preserve the predictor algorithm and backend.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a three-entry flow-through predicted-fetch queue inside if_stage.
Preserve the current 32-entry full-tag BTB policy, full target widths,
counter updates and exactly-once accepted-MEM training latency. Fetch and
retain complete predicted instruction snapshots during backend holds;
consume saved words during instruction-bus stalls. Use three separate
constant-index whole-word flop banks with entry zero always the oldest.
Store full PC, instruction, prediction_selected, full predicted_target,
valid payload and one frontier marker. Never reconstruct queued PCs.
Use prefix occupancy v0,v1,v2 and fixed shift/append bank enables.

An occupied queue presents slot zero. An empty queue presents the current
live bus word and its current BTB prediction directly, using only v0 for
payload selection. Qualify validity independently of payload bits. An
empty live word is consumed immediately if the instruction bus accepts it
and the backend can accept; do not write it into storage in that case.
If the backend holds, save the same accepted live snapshot into slot zero.
This eliminates registered-refill bubbles after recovery and ordinary
queue drain, while retaining instruction-bus acceptance during backend
holds. Decode operands only when ID accepts the selected word.

Use these controls from OLD state, all inhibited on reset/recovery:
  push = imemReady && !v2 && !frontier_wait;
  pop = v0 && backend_ready;
  bypass = !v0 && backend_ready && push;
  stored_push = push && !bypass.
Push depends on free capacity at cycle start, never on pop. An initially
full queue refuses simultaneous replacement; this keeps fetch advancement
independent of late hazard/execute readiness. Advance fetch PC once per
push, including bypass. Store the exact prediction observed at that edge.
Derive constant-bank append enables without a count or pointer subtract:
  append0 = stored_push && (!v0 || (pop && !v1));
  append1 = stored_push && ((v0 && !v1 && !pop) || (v1 && !v2 && pop));
  append2 = stored_push && v1 && !pop.
Append wins over shift. Otherwise pop shifts slot1 into slot0 and slot2 into slot1. Unwritten/invalid payloads need no reset.
Update prefix occupancy with OLD values:
  v0_next = stored_push || (v0 && !pop) || v1;
  v1_next = (v1 && !pop) || v2 || (stored_push && v0 && (!pop || v1));
  v2_next = (v2 && !pop) || (stored_push && v1 && !pop).
The only valid occupancy patterns are empty, one, two and three.
Use packed vector wires between separately generated flop banks so the
formal frontend accepts whole-word storage and synthesis avoids indexed
payload reads. A balanced two-source mask/OR can implement head/live
selection, but never qualify raw instruction/source-address bits with
redirect, bus readiness or backend readiness.

Handle raw imemReady locally in IF. Backend holds come only from the
presented instruction's load-use dependency, genuine older dmem hold and
execute_busy. An available queued head must remain consumable when the
physical bus stalls; an unavailable head inserts the existing ID bubble.
Keep all existing ID flush/hold and held-operand-refresh rules. Accepted
MEM recovery overrides frontend/backend holds, cancels push/pop/bypass,
clears occupancy and installs the full resolved target. Correct predictions
retain queued work. Learn on the existing resolving MEM event, including
its own redirect edge; queue activity and squashed instructions never train.

Bound speculative lookahead at the instruction-memory frontier. If an
accepted snapshot's predicted successor is outside [0,0x00100000), mark
that exact dynamic snapshot, save its full successor and hold the physical
fetch PC at its accepted address. Accept no duplicate words while waiting;
the queued backend drains normally. Carry the marker through ID/EX and
EX/MEM, including all pending blocking payloads. Only that exact marked
instruction's accepted-MEM event authorizes release of the saved full
successor as actual architectural demand if no recovery is required.
Recovery/reset cancel the wait; recovery has priority over release. Never
release by PC equality, clamp an architectural demand, truncate addresses
or suppress symbolic progress. Only one frontier marker may be outstanding.

Preserve nret=1, external IO, full PCs/targets, default-illegal validated
decoding, every trap, actual RVFI operands/successors, contiguous retirement
order, complete operand capture, load-use and memory handshakes, exactly-once
stores and real/ALTOPS arithmetic. The added frontier bit changes IF/ID to
99 bits, ID/EX to 329 and EX/MEM to 296; update explicit packed masks and
directed-test layouts consistently with numeric/frontend-supported widths.
Do not modify any evaluation contract. Reimplement from this description:
prototype artifacts are transient and removed before implementation/eval.
Measure canonical bracketed stalled CoreMark cycles and median vendor Fmax
together. Head/live source selection before forwarding is the main timing
risk; accepting a depth solely because it saves cycles is insufficient.

The isolated three-entry prototype passes full RVFI-to-ISS comparisons for

the final implementation. Head/live source selection ahead of forwarding is
the known timing risk and must be assessed with actual vendor reports.

title: Register complete register-file read controls at decode
motivation:
The champion scores 200.25 at median Gowin Fmax 90.355 MHz with
4,512,213 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged vendor build
reproduces that frequency and exposes closely competing ALU, predictor
maintenance and operand-delivery paths; one placement also shows MEM/WB
rd-to-register-file-to-ID/EX operand timing. Earlier r4s1 succeeded by
registering bypass provenance, r5s1 preserved real operand flops with
separate register-file word banks, and r10s1 added a decoded boundary.
That boundary now offers a place to resolve the remaining physical
register-file word selects and write-first bypass matches before the
operand data cycle. Prior micro_opt work on wide EX/MEM capture lost
4.69 percent, while r9s0 fast-result selection lost 0.59 percent. Keep
the successful datapath and optimize its read-selection controls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register all physical register-file read-selection controls at the
existing decoded-instruction boundary: a 31-bit nonzero-word select
for each source plus its one-bit match to the WB instruction that will
exist during the following operand-read cycle. This is one local
control-retiming micro_opt. Preserve the pipeline topology, instruction
latency, predictor and training policy, arithmetic units, complete
ID/EX operands, single issue and nret=1. Do not combine this with BTB,
ALU, memory-lane or fetch-queue changes.

In id_stage, decode each incoming raw source field against constant
register numbers 1 through 31 and capture those one-hot vectors on the
same edge and with the same reset/squash/replace/hold priorities as
decoded_q. Capture all zeros for invalid incoming records and x0;
hold the vectors while the decoded record is held. These are actual
flops feeding the existing constant-index register-file read leaves,
not a combinational decode of decoded_q.rs1_addr or rs2_addr. Keep
binary source addresses for RVFI, existing forwarding and x0 handling.
No packed architectural bundle changes are needed if the vectors are
exported as internal module ports.

Also compute two exact next-cycle write-first matches before that
edge. The next WB candidate is the current accepted MEM instruction:
its destination is wb_accepted.rd and its writer qualification is
!reset && !hold_mem_wb && wb_accepted.w_en. This retains final alignment
trap suppression and valid/accepted-memory qualification; it must not
use the younger EX destination or an assumed unconditional advance.
For a replacing decoded record, compare this candidate to the incoming
raw source addresses and qualify by incoming validity and nonzero rd.
For a held decoded record, compare against decoded_q's unchanged source
addresses and validity instead. Reset or accepted recovery clears both
matches. Recompute these two small match flops on EVERY nonreset edge,
including decoded holds, because WB can drain or change while the
consumer stays decoded. Do not freeze them with the word-select vector.

After the edge these match bits must be exactly equivalent to current
WB write-enable && current WB destination == decoded source && source
!= x0. An older dmem hold produces an invalid next WB record, hence
zero matches, while the previously valid WB write still commits to the
word flops on that edge. Subsequent held reads then see the committed
register-file word. A completing blocking producer, load-use bubble,
trap-suppressed write, ordinary pipeline bubble or recovery must obey
this same real MEM/WB transfer rule. Never retain a match referring to
a departed WB instruction or let a speculative fetch change a held
consumer's match. This preserves the write-first behavior used when a
producer leaves the explicit EX/MEM forwarding window.

In reg_file, retain the 31 resettable word banks, synchronous write
logic, x0 override and balanced AND/OR read trees. Feed each tree leaf
with its registered word-select bit. For the integrated core, select
the existing registered WB data with the supplied registered write-first
match instead of recomputing the live five-bit WB/source equality.
The existing EX/accepted-MEM forwarding priority over the register-file
base stays unchanged. Do not move data-word capture, add a synchronous
RAM read, or put a new late destination comparator ahead of the output.
An internal parameter may retain the original binary-address interface
as the default for standalone reg_file unit tests, with the core
explicitly enabling predecoded read controls; exercise both modes.
Neither mode may change actual stored-word writes or x0 behavior.

An isolated prototype of exactly these three RTL changes passes all

median 90.355 MHz. Option-0 resources are 5,730 LUT4 and 2,371 FF versus
5,971 and 2,307; LUT-RAM/BSRAM/DSP remain 44/4/2. The intended hardware
change adds 64 control flops and removes operand-cycle word decoding
and destination matching. The median-placement worst paths move to
registered branch successor/pending-payload formation. This is a
prototype result, not an accepted tournament measurement.

title: Isolate the frontend behind registered fetch and training ingress
motivation:
The champion's new registered decode/operand-read boundary reaches
200.25 iterations/sec at 90.355 MHz and 4,512,213 bracketed cycles.
Previous fetch queues reduced CoreMark cycles by roughly 6-8 percent,
but their head/live mux and queue controls reached operand capture
through the combined decode stage. In particular, r10s2 cut cycles
7.51 percent but its flow-through head selection limited Fmax to
78.635 MHz. The current separate decoded register creates a new place
to isolate a strictly registered fetch head from operand delivery.
Isolated probes expose competing frontend limits: a training row-read
pipeline clears the reported 27-cell BTB maintenance path and reaches
91.762 MHz, but gains only 1.56 percent fitness. A strictly registered
fetch queue cuts cycles 4.78 percent but reaches only 86.632 MHz and
gains 0.69 percent fitness. Neither clears acceptance individually.
Registering both frontend ingress paths can combine stall overlap
with removal of the maintenance cone. This is a proposed joint
frontend structure, not a claim that either isolated probe wins.

fetch stage, implemented as three

no head/live word mux, no PC reconstruction and no indexed RAM read
feeding decode. Keep the champion's separate decoded metadata and

also captures the selected row state before ordered update, so both

Separate queue-to-decode acceptance from instruction-bus acceptance.

current record, independently of current imemReady. Pass operand-read

dequeue decision. Fetch may enqueue during load-use, genuine dmem

using local occupancy only; sustain one dequeue and one enqueue per

title: Pipeline BTB tag probing before local direction-state updates
motivation:
The current champion scores 200.25 at 90.355 MHz with 4,512,213 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at EX/MEM's registered
resolution PC and ends at a predictor direction counter, crossing 27
cells in 17.811 ns. The selected tag/counter read, full tag comparison,
saturating arithmetic and indexed write qualification are still one
predictor-maintenance cone. Earlier fetch queues reduced cycles but
slowed operand delivery, and the round-seven all-flop BTB slowed fetch
lookup through parallel full-tag fanout. Preserve the existing indexed
fetch lookup and instead isolate and simplify predictor training.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming only BTB maintenance should remove the measured counter-update
bottleneck without adding instruction pipeline stages or fetch queues.
Keep the 32-entry fully tagged target buffer, indexed fetch tag/target
reads, full PC/target widths, current prediction snapshots and existing
accepted-MEM recovery latency. Probe the training tag into one registered
event stage inside if_stage, then apply its update independently. Implement
direction state as separate constant-index two-flop banks with local
transition equations. Keep tag/target arrays
indexed; do not reproduce the rejected parallel full-tag fetch tree.

Each accepted MEM training event captures valid, PC index/full tag,
aligned eligibility, jump classification, actual outcome, aligned
full target and an ordered tag-hit result. The previous event applies
on the next clock while a new event is captured, sustaining one event
per clock. Events drain despite
frontend holds and bus stalls; a redirect preserves its resolving
instruction's event. Reset clears event validity and all BTB valid bits.
Do not delay redirect, retirement, execution, or architectural effects.
Capture event payload only when train_valid is asserted; event_valid_q
itself captures train_valid every nonreset clock so bubbles drain it.
Use a five-bit event_index_q, 25-bit event_tag_q, 30-bit event_target_q,
and event_valid_q/event_eligible_q/event_jump_q/event_taken_q/event_hit_q.
Only event_valid_q needs reset; all table-update gates also reject reset.

Encode each direction counter as direction D and strength S:
strongly-not-taken=(0,1), weakly-not-taken=(0,0), weakly-taken=(1,0),
strongly-taken=(1,1). A matching conditional event with outcome T uses
D_next = S ? D : T and S_next = (D == T), both from OLD local state.
A miss allocates D=T,S=0; a jump writes D=1,S=1. These equations exactly
implement the existing two-bit saturation without a selected counter
read, adder or saturation comparator on the write path. Decode the
registered event index against each constant bank. The fetch direction
remains an indexed read of D; fetch never needs S. Keep tags and targets
as the original indexed storage. Counter application uses the registered
tag-hit bit, so no tag read or tag comparison is ahead of the local
counter update. Do not capture old counter values: local state at
application already includes every earlier applied event.
The tested storage shape uses two packed 32-bit vectors direction_q
and strength_q, written one constant-index bit per generated bank.
Each bank updates only on !reset && event_valid_q && event_eligible_q
&& event_index_q == its constant index. Lookup reads direction_q from
the existing fetch_index; valid_q, tags and targets retain the original
indexed organization. Invalid counter/tag/target payloads need no reset.
Do not register a 32-bit bank-write mask: that measured slower.

Make the captured tag-hit describe the logical table AFTER the older
pending event applies on the same edge. Start with valid[train_index]
and tags[train_index] == train_pc[31:7]. When the older event is valid
and addresses the same index, an eligible older event replaces this hit
with older_event_tag == train_pc[31:7]. An ineligible older event with
its own registered hit clears this hit, reflecting its invalidation;
an ineligible older miss leaves it unchanged. This one-entry ordered
forwarding covers replacement, reallocation and invalidation without
exposing outcomes to fetch. Register the resulting probe hit with the
event. All table writes come from this event stage, so its saved hit is
authoritative at application. Consecutive same-index events observe all
earlier writes; delayed invalidation cannot erase another PC's entry.

Train exactly once from the existing train_valid accepted-MEM event.
Preserve legal/aligned control-transfer eligibility, weak conditional
allocation, strongly-taken jump updates and tag-qualified stale-entry
invalidation. Train on the resolving redirect edge, never from squashed
younger work or a held MEM record. Fetch sees committed predictor state
only; do not bypass a live outcome or pending update into lookup. The
additional learning cycle may increase short-loop misses, but the
unchanged architectural mismatch recovery corrects every stale outcome,
stale noncontrol prediction, changed JALR target and trapped transfer.
Prediction metadata stays attached to its original dynamic instruction
throughout holds, blocking completion and squash.

Preserve nret=1, all external ports, default-illegal validated decoding,
full RVFI operands and resolved successors, contiguous retirement order,
arithmetic/ALTOPS behavior, memory handshakes and exactly-once stores.
The single angle is predictor-maintenance timing; leave operand capture,
recovery calculation, frontend delivery and prediction algorithm alone.
Require the unchanged formal, unit, stalled ISS cosim and canonical

median vendor Fmax above approximately 94.511 MHz. Measure cycles and Gowin timing
together because extra learning latency and competing paths can erase
a frequency gain. No evaluation-contract changes are proposed.

title: Fuse registered one-hot fast-result choices into execute capture

The champion scores 223.34 iterations/sec at median Gowin Fmax 95.961
MHz and 4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path
runs from complete ID/EX operands through the ALU and EX result
selection to data memory. An untouched placement-0 rebuild reproduces
88.343 MHz and the 16.618 ns path exactly; it traverses shift/result,
jump-link, input-valid and emission selection. A dedicated-address
probe removes that endpoint but falls to median 89.055 MHz as operand
delivery becomes limiting, so specialization alone is insufficient.
Earlier r9s0 explored predecoded fast result selection: its temporary
prototype gained 7.18 percent, but the final experiment regressed
0.59 percent with a decode/immediate critical path. The current true
decoded and fetch register boundaries isolate that former competing
cone, making fused result selection worth evaluating on this champion.

title: Balance registered execution across decode, operand read, and EX
motivation: The champion reaches 223.34 iterations/sec at median 95.961 MHz and 4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported critical path begins at complete ID/EX operands and reaches FPGA data memory through the shared ALU and EX capture logic. Previous structural work successfully isolated slow M arithmetic, complete operands, decoded metadata, and frontend ingress. The existing decoded stage now creates an unused opportunity to pre-read the register file before operand resolution, allowing short arithmetic work to move across the operand/EX boundary without adding a stage. A current-parent memory-lane probe regressed to 90.471 MHz; simply precomputing 16-bit half-sums after the existing RF read regressed to 63.290 MHz. Thus repartition the existing stages together: first register RF snapshots, then compute short resolved-operand chunks, then finish execution.
