hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the work of the existing decode, operand-read, and EX stages, retaining their number and every instruction-transfer boundary. The new topology is registered fetch head -> decode plus RF snapshots -> forwarding plus eight-bit arithmetic partials -> EX carry selection and result capture -> MEM -> WB. This is one structural pipeline-balancing change; do not add a cache, predictor policy, general issue stage, or instruction bubble.

During decode capture, read the existing flop-bank register file using the registered fetch head's raw rs1/rs2 fields. Register both read words alongside the matching decoded metadata. Keep the explicit resettable RF word flops and balanced trees; avoid inferred RAM that absorbs downstream operand registers. Raw head fields drive only this earlier RF lookup, never the late EX operand mux. The RF's existing current-WB write-first behavior applies to these reads. Capture or hold the snapshots with the same decoded record, and clear them on reset/accepted recovery.

At operand resolution, use the captured RF snapshots as base values instead of traversing the RF word-selection tree again. A newer current MEM/WB writer may have appeared after the snapshot: retain an explicit qualified current-WB-over-snapshot bypass, matching the held decoded source address and excluding x0. During every decoded hold, refresh a matching snapshot from an actual qualified WB write so a departed producer cannot be lost. title: Banked hashed BTB with taken-only allocation preserves useful targets
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 with 4,296,564 timed CoreMark cycles at
95.961 MHz. Its 32-entry direct-mapped bimodal predictor produces 73,619
accepted control-transfer recoveries in the measured interval: 55,992
conditional branches, 15,638 direct jumps and 1,989 returns. Hot direct
jumps repeatedly miss, showing target conflicts rather than a return-stack
opportunity. Every legal conditional branch currently allocates a row,
even on a not-taken miss that needs no target, evicting useful taken paths.
Earlier attempts mostly changed delivery or maintenance timing, and the
champion already has registered fetch and training boundaries. Focus this
attempt solely on retaining useful predictor entries under conflicts.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 32-entry tagged bimodal BTB with one conflict-resistant
128-entry predictor: four indexed 32-entry banks, a reversible XOR index,
and taken-only allocation on a tag miss. Compute the seven-bit index as
PC[8:2] XOR PC[15:9], use index[6:5] as the bank and index[4:0] as its row,
and retain the entire PC[31:9] tag and 30 aligned target bits. This is a
full tag: PC[15:9] is contained in the stored tag, so the tag and hashed
index uniquely reconstruct PC[31:2]. Do not use partial tags or shorten
targets. Mixing address bits disperses hot code with repeated low offsets;
taken-only allocation stops irrelevant not-taken misses from replacing
useful targets. These are one predictor-conflict policy, with no changes
to frontend delivery, direction algorithm, recovery timing or execution.

A matching legal conditional branch still updates its existing two-bit
counter for either outcome, using the current Boolean saturation equations.
A conditional miss allocates weakly taken only when actually taken. A
not-taken conditional miss leaves the entire addressed row untouched:
validity, tag, target and counter. Legal aligned JAL/JALR allocate or update
strongly taken as before. Ineligible events retain exact tag-qualified
stale-entry invalidation, without erasing another PC's replacement. The
allocation decision must gate both table writes and the logical post-update
row used for forwarding; merely suppressing the write while forwarding an
imaginary allocation is incorrect.

Declare each bank's tag, target and counter arrays separately with 32 rows
inside a constant-index generate block. Read each bank with the five-bit
row index, then select the bank with a balanced four-way selection. Keep
indexed RAM-friendly storage, rather than parallel full-tag comparison
against 128 flop words or a single dynamically indexed 128-row array.
Preserve all existing fetch and training register boundaries and latency.
Extend the training event and row snapshot index to seven bits. Forward
the older event's complete post-update row only when its entire hashed
index matches the incoming event. This includes skipped allocations,
replacement, counter update and invalidation. Same row number in different
banks is independent. Commit one edge after accepted-MEM capture, exactly
as today, sustaining one event per clock. Training proceeds across frontend
holds; recovery preserves the resolving event and reset clears all bank
validity and cancels pending training.

Keep the three fixed fetch records and enqueue/dequeue schedule unchanged.
Capture selected/target predictions with the exact accepted bus word and
retain them through queue, decoded and EX holds. The actual successor and
existing accepted-MEM recovery remain authoritative for every instruction,
including stale noncontrol entries, illegal instructions, misaligned
transfers and changed JALR targets. Preserve nret=1 external ports,
default-illegal decoding, operand forwarding, blocking arithmetic,
ALTOPS behavior, contiguous RVFI order and exactly-once memory handshakes.
Require the unchanged formal, stalled ISS cosim and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker/OOB gates. Judge median Gowin Fmax times bracketed
iterations/cycle; acceptance requires fitness above 233.61 iterations/sec.

Exploratory evidence: a fresh unmodified champion run reproduces exactly
4,296,564 timed cycles. Straight expansion to an unbanked 128-row array
uses 4,228,278 cycles but measures only 95.003 MHz median, insufficient for
acceptance. Taken-only allocation with the original 32-entry organization
uses 4,221,644 cycles. Both simulations complete with all canonical CRCs,
success UART, valid markers and no OOB. Correct-path replay estimates
43,641 control-transfer misses for the proposed hashed 128-entry taken-only
policy versus the measured 73,619 in the champion. Replay ignores learning
latency and wrong-path fetch and is not a measured cycle or fitness gain.
Explicit 32-row banking is essential because the unbanked capacity probe
inferred extra BSRAM and exposed tag-read-to-valid-update timing paths.
Reproduce the proposed combined policy and measure its actual cycle count
and median vendor timing; exploratory artifacts are not implementation
inputs and do not establish tournament acceptance.

title: Balance branch comparisons with parallel byte relation summaries
motivation: The champion scores 223.34 iterations/sec at median Fmax 95.961 MHz with 4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. An untouched placement-0 rebuild reproduces 88.343 MHz. Its five worst paths include a 16.574 ns, 37-cell path from registered rs2 bit zero through EX into the pending next-PC register, alongside the ALU and operand-capture paths. Local carry-prefix, duplicated shifter-bank and several shared right-shifter probes failed to improve the three-option median. Branch comparisons still use wide signed/unsigned relational operators; a balanced comparison can shorten their carry-dependent resolution without moving arithmetic onto the memory-return path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the EX branch relation datapath with four parallel eight-bit unsigned comparisons and a balanced two-level combination of equality/less-than summaries. This is a local branch-comparator micro_opt, preserving the pipeline, predictor, issue/retirement width and every instruction latency.

For bytes i=0..3 compute eq[i] = rs1[8*i +: 8] == rs2[8*i +: 8] and lt[i] = rs1[8*i +: 8] < rs2[8*i +: 8]. Byte 3 is most significant. Form low_lt = lt[1] OR (eq[1] AND lt[0]) and high_lt = lt[3] OR (eq[3] AND lt[2]) in parallel. Then unsigned_lt = high_lt OR (eq[3] AND eq[2] AND low_lt). Form signed_lt = (rs1[31] != rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : unsigned_lt, and equal_word = AND-reduction(eq). BEQ/BNE use equal_word and its inverse; BLT/BGE use signed_lt and its inverse; BLTU/BGEU use unsigned_lt and its inverse. Preserve the branch-op default false. Use explicit fixed-width slices and this balanced grouping, not a serial byte-priority chain or a newly inferred 32-bit subtraction.

All inputs remain the original complete registered EX rs1_val/rs2_val. The comparator feeds the existing branch_cond, branch_taken, target/trap qualification, resolved next-PC and registered recovery exactly where the original comparator did. Preserve legal control-target alignment traps, jump/JALR handling, launch/consume priorities, pending instruction metadata and prediction snapshots, exactly-once accepted-MEM recovery/training, genuine memory holds and dominant squash/reset. Do not resolve branches in an earlier stage or add an extra resolution cycle. Keep the ALU, register file, forwarding, load extraction, fetch queue and predictor policy unchanged, including both real and ALTOPS RV32M arithmetic. Keep nret=1 and every top-level port and RVFI field.

The four independent narrow carry chains followed by two relation-combine levels should shorten signed/unsigned branch resolution and reduce duplicated comparison logic. Equality is shared across all branch functions. This trades a small amount of local logic for less serial comparator depth; Gowin remapping, routing and the competing ALU/RF/load-return paths remain uncertainties. Expect a six-percent timing-driven fitness gain with unchanged bracketed cycles and low confidence until full vendor evaluation. No accepted improvement is claimed. At unchanged cycles the required median Fmax is above 100.375206 MHz and fitness above 233.61364.

Add exact tests for all six branch functions with equal operands, every byte position as the highest differing byte, lower-byte differences that oppose the higher-byte relation, unsigned high-bit operands, signed extrema and deterministic random pairs. Test true and false outcomes, original prediction snapshots, aligned/misaligned targets, back-to-back resolving branches, load/ALU-produced operands, long bus holds, blocking completion and accepted older recovery. Check exact successors, traps, RVFI operands and contiguous order, and no younger side effects. title: Repartition register reads and persistent producer routing before execution
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 at median 95.961 MHz and 4,296,564 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path traverses the general execute result
selection into data RAM. A current-parent dedicated LSU request probe
removes that endpoint but reaches only 89.542 MHz, exposing both live
load-return forwarding and dmemReady-to-operand/provenance control.
Registering raw memory returns passes stalled ISS and CoreMark CRCs,
but adds 4.94 percent cycles and regresses median Fmax to 82.758 MHz;
it still leaves dmemReady driving operand capture. Therefore the next
structural target is the coupling of producer values to transaction
acceptance, rather than another load-return or arithmetic stage.
The earlier r9s1 immutable-operand attempt was limited by bus-to-decode
and target-match logic; the current registered decode and fixed fetch
head have since isolated that older competing frontend cone. A probe
combining persistent producer values with the dedicated request lane
preserves the champion's cycles and passes stalled ISS/CRC checks, but
reaches only 94.536 MHz. Its median placement exposes RF lookup into
operand capture. Thus the proposed complete repartition moves RF reads
into the existing decode edge as well, while keeping arithmetic after
complete operand storage; none of these isolated probes claims a win.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the existing decode, operand-read and execute boundaries
so decode captures RF base values, operand read selects persistent
producer values, and execute owns scalar arithmetic and a separately
registered memory request lane. No stage or instruction latency is
added. This is one pipeline topology change with three balanced roles,
rather than precomputing arithmetic after incoming load data.
Operand selection uses the instruction owning a producer position;
bus readiness and consume events control movement of instruction
records, not whether the producer's 32-bit value enters a bypass mux.
Keep every stage boundary, normal/load/M latency, frontend policy and
in-order retirement width. Do not add a raw-return stage or arithmetic
before the complete ID/EX operand flops.

Form a dedicated LSU address ADD from complete captured operands,
with independent request-address storage. Register store replication,
lane mask, read/write eligibility and alignment qualification with
the request at the same edge. Drive the timed memory interface from
these fields, keeping the general scalar operation, jump-link and
blocking-completion result selections out of the address path. Use
the dedicated address consistently for load extraction and RVFI.
Request side effects still depend on actual fast instruction advance;
stalls hold the complete packet, and recovery cancels younger packets.

Separately make fast arithmetic, direct-jump link, pending completion
and MEM final-data candidates continuously observable while their
owning records occupy the corresponding producer positions. Fast
eligibility depends on registered instruction validity, register-write
intent, nonload status, nonblocking operation and target legality.
Link eligibility additionally selects a direct jump. Pending-result
ownership requires the pending-valid bit, original captured destination
and trap-qualified write intent; clear ownership on consume/reset/
recovery even though its old payload remains stored. These candidate
kinds must be mutually exclusive for an EX-position source match.
In particular, a blocking MUL/DIV/JALR must never select the ordinary
fast ALU output, and a consumed completion must never remain a writer.

Remove fast_emit, link_emit, completed_emit and wb_accept from the
operand data-selection masks. Use registered source provenance plus
producer ownership, operation kind, nonzero destination and final
trap qualification. Keep youngest-writer priority and independent
older matches so a suppressed trapping writer exposes the right older
value. MEM can expose its load/ALU value without io_dmemReady in its
data mask: a genuine older memory wait already prevents operand
capture. A pending M result may change before done, but execute_busy
prevents capture until the exact completion is ready. No unavailable
load or pending result is ever accepted, and loads never forward
effective addresses as register data.

Retain the current late handshake controls for actual EX/MEM emission,
unit request/consume, MEM acceptance, predictor training, retirement
and physical writes. They also govern the operand register bank's
capture/hold/clear, with reset and accepted recovery dominant. Accepted
operands remain immutable during holds. Separate value ownership from
those transfer events explicitly in interfaces and comments; do not
rename an emit signal while retaining its dmemReady dependence in the
data-selection cone. Keep early destination comparison and provenance
rebasing associated with actual next producer positions through holds,
load-use bubbles and completion. Values from departed producers must
remain recoverable through write-first RF reads.

This is one producer/consumer pipeline repartition: early RF snapshots
and autonomous result lanes feed operand selection, while the request
lane controls memory side effects and stage movement. It aims to break the repeatedly exposed memory-
readiness-to-wide-bypass cone together with the scalar-result-to-memory
cone, without paying an extra load-use cycle. The request-only probe
is a negative control, not evidence that the combined partition wins.

original RVFI operands/PCs, contiguous order and exactly-once effects.

title: Predict direct targets from instruction immediates with a direction-only table
motivation:
The champion incurs 73,619 accepted control-transfer recoveries in
4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its shared 32-entry BTB loses direct
JAL targets to conflicts and ties conditional direction learning to
target residency. Enlarging and hashing target storage in r12s2 saved
3.09 percent of cycles but reduced median Fmax to 85.308 MHz. Direct
branch and JAL targets already reside in instruction immediates; using
them avoids expanding the wide tag/target lookup and reserves target
storage for the indirect transfers that actually need it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict direct control transfers from the accepted instruction word,
decoupling conditional direction from target storage. In IF recognize
JAL and validated BRANCH funct3 values, expand their J/B immediates,
and use one shared PC-plus-immediate adder to compute the direct target.
Always predict an aligned JAL taken. For a legal conditional branch,
choose direction from a separate 512-entry untagged two-bit bimodal
table indexed by PC[10:2], and use the instruction-derived target when
taken. Implement the two-bit counters as an indexed RAM without a
payload reset, with a separate resettable initialized-bit vector. An
uninitialized row reads as weakly not taken, 01; fetch predicts not
taken until the row's first committed update. Reset clears initialized
bits and pending training, rather than resetting all 1024 counter bits.
Invalid branch
funct3 values never use direct prediction. Suppress direct prediction
on a misaligned target; the existing architectural resolver retains
full authority over trapping and the actual successor.

Retain the original 32-entry indexed full-tag/full-target BTB only for
legal aligned JALR training. Direct JAL and conditional branches never
allocate target rows. A non-JALR event invalidates a matching obsolete
indirect entry using the existing full-tag check; it must not erase a
conflicting PC's entry. For words other than direct JAL/legal BRANCH,
preserve BTB prediction and existing stale-hit recovery, including on
noncontrol and illegal instructions. Select direct targets and the
existing indirect target path in parallel, never by a larger target RAM
or additional bank/hash hierarchy. Keep full 32-bit architectural PCs.

Train the direction table only on legal aligned conditional branches
accepted by MEM, exactly once. Capture its nine-bit index, outcome and
old two-bit counter behind a register boundary; commit the Boolean
saturating transition one edge later. Consecutive events at the same
direction index forward the older complete post-update counter,
including events from different PCs that alias in this untagged table.
Do not update direction on JAL, JALR, bubbles, held MEM records or
squashed younger work. Reset cancels pending training and makes every
direction row logically weakly not taken; recovery preserves the resolving event and
older commit. Direction and indirect training run independently of
frontend queue occupancy and backend holds.

Preserve all three fixed registered fetch positions and their transfer
schedule. Snapshot selected/target metadata with each accepted bus
instruction, using the same selection that advances fetch PC; never
recompute queued predictions from subsequently trained state. Retain
all decode/operand/EX holds, complete operands, blocking arithmetic,
accepted-MEM recovery and target-match registers. Keep nret=1, external
ports, default-illegal decoding, RVFI operands and resolved successors,
contiguous order, arithmetic/ALTOPS and exactly-once memory handshakes.
Run unchanged formal, unit, stalled ISS cosim and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker/OOB gates. Judge bracketed cycles times median Gowin
Fmax; acceptance requires fitness above 233.61 iterations/second.

only 155 additional misses, so choose 512 entries. Private local history
was rejected after replay increased misses. These are sizing estimates;
replay omits wrong-path fetch, training latency and stall overlap, and
does not establish an RTL cycle reduction or an FPGA frequency gain.

title: Use byte carry-select ADD/SUB entirely inside registered execute
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 iterations/sec at median Gowin Fmax
95.961 MHz and 4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported
worst path starts at a complete ID/EX ALU operand and passes through
the fast ALU and EX capture to data memory. r12s1's carry-select
arithmetic was moved before ID/EX and worsened the memory-return
path to 22.22 ns; that failure argues for preserving complete operand
flops, not for performing arithmetic in operand read. Prior local
carry-prefix probes also failed, so use speculative byte sums with
explicit carry selection rather than another bit-prefix adder.

hypothesis.motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the fast ALU's ADD and SUB implementations with one
shared four-byte carry-select datapath, entirely after the existing
complete ID/EX operand flops and before the original EX/MEM edge.
This is a local arithmetic micro_opt. Preserve all pipeline stages,
register boundaries, instruction latencies, forwarding controls,
memory formatting, register file, predictor and bus acceptance.

Let subtract = (op == ALU_SUB), B = b XOR {32{subtract}}, and initial
carry C0 = subtract. For each byte i=0..3 independently calculate
two explicitly nine-bit unsigned sums:
  S0[i] = {0,a[8*i +: 8]} + {0,B[8*i +: 8]}
  S1[i] = {0,a[8*i +: 8]} + {0,B[8*i +: 8]} + 9'd1.
Each local arithmetic chain is eight bits; no byte's sum depends
on the preceding byte's carry. Define G[i]=S0[i][8] and T[i]=S1[i][8].
T is the carry-out for carry-in one, not necessarily pure propagate.
The exact carry transfer is Cnext = G OR (T AND Cprevious).

Compute the three selecting carries with expanded parallel Boolean
expressions rather than a serial recurrence:
  C1 = G0 OR (T0 AND C0)
  C2 = G1 OR (T1 AND G0) OR (T1 AND T0 AND C0)
  C3 = G2 OR (T2 AND G1) OR (T2 AND T1 AND G0)
       OR (T2 AND T1 AND T0 AND C0).
Use balanced grouping where it helps LUT4 mapping. Select each
output byte from S1[i][7:0] when Ci is one, otherwise S0[i][7:0].
Discard final carry to implement exact modulo-2^32 RV32 ADD/SUB.
Keep explicit widths so contextual sizing cannot truncate a carry.
Preserve the existing ALU operation case and its default zero;
both ADD and SUB use this result, all other operations keep their
current implementations. Do not register partial sums in decode or
operand read and do not share the new adder with branch comparison.

The change bounds local carry propagation and replaces a full-word
carry dependency with a short Boolean carry-selection network. It
trades duplicate byte sums and selection LUTs for less arithmetic
depth. Loads/stores and JALR still get their addresses from the same
fast ADD operation with the same accepted operands. Preserve the
existing link result, control-target alignment handling, pending
payloads, launch/consume, genuine memory holds, accepted MEM recovery/
training and retirement timing. Keep nret=1 and all external ports,
full addresses, exact RVFI operands/results/successors/order,
default-illegal decode and SYSTEM policy. Multiplication, division,
all ALTOPS formulas, memory masks/traps and exactly-once side effects
remain unchanged.

Estimate six percent timing-driven fitness gain with low confidence.
Gowin may merge the speculative sums back into a ripple chain, or
competing branch/load-return/readiness paths may limit benefit.
Inspect mapped arithmetic and compare all three vendor placement
options, LUT/FF use and bracketed cycles. At unchanged cycles the
acceptance threshold is median Fmax above 100.375206 MHz and fitness
above 233.61364. No candidate timing improvement is claimed until
the isolated carry-select probe's vendor builds complete.

Validate ADD/SUB against independent modulo-32-bit integer arithmetic:
zero, all ones, signed extrema, byte-boundary carries/borrows,
propagating carries through one to four bytes, alternating bits,
all byte carry-generation/propagation combinations and deterministic
random operand pairs. Check ordinary ALU consumers, load/store
effective addresses, AUIPC and JALR under bus stalls with exact RVFI
operands, results, successors and alignment traps. Retain every
existing test; require unchanged formal, stalled ISS cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker checks and measured bracketed
cycles. Do not credit RVFI-only pruning or an isolated placement
variation as a fitness improvement.

title: Integrate synchronous register-file reads into one operand capture network
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 with median Gowin Fmax 95.961 MHz and
4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its register file contains 31
resettable 32-bit word banks and two large combinational masked-OR
read trees, followed by write-first selection and operand forwarding.
The earlier r5s1 flop-bank change won because it prevented inferred RAM
read ports from absorbing the complete execution operand registers.
There is now a separate registered decoded stage, introduced by r10s1,
where synchronous register-file reads can end without absorbing those
execution flops. r11s0's early one-hot selects gained only 5.22 percent;
r13s1's early snapshots plus persistent routing and an LSU lane lost
8.77 percent. r12s1's precomputed arithmetic lost 22.57 percent by putting
addition after incoming load data. These results motivate changing the
register-file storage/read boundary alone, with unchanged execution,
forwarding policy, memory latency, predictor and stage count.
A synchronous-read component probe passes 53 unchanged fast formal
checks, all 51 existing pipeline cases, eight instruction cosims and
canonical stalled CoreMark validation at exactly 4,296,564 bracketed
cycles. It infers two additional BSRAMs, reduces logic from 6204 to
4586 and registers from 2689 to 1806, and reaches median 98.737 MHz
across placements 91.406/98.737/98.737. This 2.89 percent component
gain is below acceptance. The final proposal additionally integrates
RF read/correction selection with operand forwarding; the complete
candidate has not been timed and no accepted gain is claimed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the asynchronous flop-bank register file with two identical
synchronous-read, single-write memory banks, one per source port.
Both copies receive every qualified architectural write. Launch reads
using the fixed registered fetch head's source addresses on the same
edge that accepts that instruction into decoded_q. Each memory read
ends in a genuine registered output associated with that decoded
instruction; operand-read then resolves producers and captures the
existing complete ID/EX operands. Preserve a fully registered decode
boundary and complete execution operand flops, with no empty-stage
bypass. No pipeline stage, load-use bubble or normal instruction cycle

RAMs; the intended Gowin implementation is two BSRAM read/write banks.
Confirm the inferred primitive and register boundaries in vendor
synthesis instead of assuming an attribute guarantees this mapping.

Do not reset the RAM data arrays. Preserve the existing zero-after-reset
behavior through a resettable 31-bit architectural written bitmap and
registered read-valid bits; x0 always returns zero and ignores writes.
Same-edge read/write collisions must explicitly return the new WB value,
independent of the physical RAM's collision mode. Capture a collision
flag and the corresponding WB word beside each synchronous read; select
this registered correction over the raw RAM output. Keep correction
logic outside the RAM read process so it cannot prevent inference.
Retain complete 32-bit values and all 32 architectural register indices.

Associate held source addresses, read-valid bits and correction state
with decoded_q. Disable new reads when decoded_q cannot be replaced.
While that instruction is held, every qualified WB write matching its
nonzero source must update its registered correction word, including
writes that make a formerly unwritten register valid. Corrections hold
after the producer retires. When a new decoded instruction is accepted,
replace correction state with that instruction's collision/valid state;
reset and accepted recovery invalidate the old association. In the
operand-read cycle, preserve a current-WB write-first bypass as well:
a writer retiring one edge after read launch must be visible immediately
to a consumer accepted into ID/EX at that edge. Reads on the reset or
squash edge cannot advertise stale architectural data.

Expose the raw registered RAM words, their registered validity, held
correction words/flags and current-WB matches as separate operand-read
candidates. Incorporate their mutually exclusive selection into the
existing final forwarding masked-OR network, including the parallel
complete ALU operand selections. Avoid selecting raw, corrected and
current-WB words into an intermediate RF base word before forwarding.
For each nonzero source, qualified EX takes priority over accepted MEM;
otherwise current WB takes priority over the retained RF correction,
then the valid raw synchronous read, then zero. Preserve this same
priority for raw RVFI operands and complete ALU operands, with PC and
immediate selecting independently as today. This preserves exactly
the architectural priority of the component probe while removing
serial RF correction/base selection from complete operand capture.
Keep acceptance controls on existing producer eligibility and bank
capture; do not also switch to persistent producer ownership. The final
candidate is this unified synchronous-read operand stage, not the

Keep the existing registered EX/MEM provenance, youngest qualified
producer priority, trap write suppression, load-use interlock and

only the base source words used when no younger producer qualifies.
An unavailable youngest load or blocking result must still prevent
operand acceptance; it must never fall back to an older RF snapshot.
Arithmetic remains strictly after complete operand storage. Do not
also add persistent producer routing, an LSU request lane, precomputed
arithmetic, a raw load-return stage or a prediction-policy change.

This single structural change moves the RF lookup to the existing

six percent gain is a projection for the complete integrated stage,
not the measured component: RAM clock-to-output, a larger final source
mux, current-WB repair and unchanged EX/predictor paths can limit it.

title: Instruction-qualified compact signatures reduce target-predictor conflicts
motivation:
The champion's 32-entry fully tagged BTB has 73,619 CoreMark control
recoveries in 4,296,564 timed cycles. Recent capacity/hash expansion
saved 3.09 percent of cycles but reduced median Gowin Fmax to 85.308
MHz; instruction-derived targets saved 3.32 percent but needed an IF
target adder and increased area. The existing precise successor check
already makes prediction aliases recoverable. Replacing full predictor
tags with two-bit signatures and qualifying predictions with the fetched
instruction can shorten lookup and maintenance while retaining the
original target-table size. This avoids the area and routing cost that
defeated larger predictor probes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the fully tagged 32-entry BTB with a 32-entry compact-signature
target predictor qualified by the actual accepted instruction word.
Keep full aligned 30-bit targets, a two-bit signature PC[8:7], one
initialized bit and a two-bit saturating counter per row. Index both
fetch and training with PC[6:2] XOR PC[10:6].
Use one indexed target array, not a bank-selection hierarchy or a
parallel full-tag comparison tree. There is no IF target adder and no
instruction-word bypass into decode. This is one predictor organization
change; retain all pipeline, queue, recovery and arithmetic timing.

Predecode only legal conditional BRANCH funct3 values, JAL, and JALR
with funct3=0. A qualified control instruction selects the stored full
target only when the indexed row is initialized, its two-bit signature
matches, and counter[1] is set; otherwise fetch PC+4. All other instructions predict PC+4 regardless of
predictor contents. Only an accepted enqueue snapshots this selection
and target and advances PC. Prediction metadata remains immutable with
its dynamic instruction through all queue and pipeline holds. Table
contents never certify instruction legality or architectural targets.

Train only legal aligned control transfers at the current accepted-MEM
event, exactly once, with the current registered ingress and one-edge
delayed commit. A matching conditional branch saturating-increments or
decrements the counter according to its outcome. A taken conditional
branch writes its full actual target and signature; a taken signature
miss allocates weakly taken. A not-taken signature miss leaves the entire
row untouched. Matching not-taken updates retain the stored target.
JAL/JALR write their actual full target, signature and strongly taken
state. The signature is intentionally lossy: matching signatures from
different full PCs may share state and require recovery. Ordinary, decoder-illegal or
misaligned events do not update or invalidate any row. A changed word
that remains a control transfer is repaired by precise recovery and
subsequent legal training. Reset clears initialized bits and pending
events; uninitialized targets/counters cannot select a prediction.

Snapshot the selected row signature, counter and initialized state at
training ingress. For consecutive events at the same entire hashed index,
forward the older event's complete logical post-update state, including
skipped allocation. Update with the existing Boolean saturation
equations rather than introducing a counter carry chain. Commits and
ingress continue independently of queue occupancy and backend holds;

title: Qualify execute payload and operand forwarding once at capture
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 at 95.961 MHz with 4,296,564 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent paths repeatedly cross dmem readiness,
producer qualification and wide operand capture. EX currently zeros
every payload word with in.valid before masking it again with
fast_emit; forwarding also gates words with transfer events even
when those same events already inhibit operand capture. r8s0's
validity-mask removal gained 4.45 percent on an older champion,
narrowly below acceptance. r13s1 bundled persistent routing with
RF snapshots and an LSU lane and regressed. Isolate the redundant
control qualification here, preserving every pipeline boundary.

A control-only prototype passes all 51 existing pipeline cases,
eight unchanged ISS cosims and canonical stalled CoreMark at exactly
4,296,564 bracketed cycles. It measures median Gowin 96.490 MHz
versus a reproduced champion 95.961 MHz, only 0.55 percent higher
and below acceptance. The final proposal also removes the redundant
EX payload-valid mask in this same capture-qualification optimization.
Probes of registered load formats, fused RF selection and registered
RF read controls regressed and are excluded from the final design.

The prototype with both ownership qualification and unconditional EX
payload construction measures 90.029/97.913/97.913 MHz, median
97.913 MHz: 2.03 percent above the champion and still below acceptance.
It uses 6037 LUT4 and 2689 FF versus 6204/2689, passes all 51 pipeline
cases and the unchanged direct-EX suite, eight instruction ISS cosims
and canonical stalled CoreMark at 4,296,564 cycles. The control-only
component also passes all 53 unchanged fast formal checks in a private
copy of the framework; the final combined design still needs formal.
The proposal below adds an unmeasured capture-selection refinement;
these prototype results are evidence about its components, not a win.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply validity and handshake authorization once at each state
acceptance boundary instead of also using them as serial data muxes.
This is one local control-factoring micro_opt. Preserve pipeline
topology, all instruction latencies, the current RF, load formatter,
ALU, multiplier/divider, fetch queue, predictor and nret=1.

In EX construct every payload field unconditionally from the complete
registered instruction and operands. Assign payload.valid = in.valid
explicitly and preserve all original target/trap/result calculations.
Remove the outer if(in.valid) zeroing of the entire payload. Keep the
existing mutually exclusive held/completed/fast masked-OR reg_d and
all current emission conditions. fast_emit already requires in.valid
and actual instruction advance; therefore every non-emitting EX/MEM
bubble still becomes exactly zero. A pending payload is captured only
on a genuine valid blocking launch, so unconditional construction
does not expose invalid work to completion. Do not change capture
priorities, pending metadata, writer suppression or recovery rules.

For the final EX/MEM alu_result input, combine result-kind and fast
emission controls before masking words. Override only reg_d.alu_result
with four parallel terms: held reg_q.alu_result under held_emit,
completed_payload.alu_result under completed_emit, the native binary-
decoded alu_result under fast_emit && !in.ctrl.is_jump, and PC+4
under fast_emit && in.ctrl.is_jump. This removes the separate wide
jump-link data mux before the emission mask. Keep every other field's
existing masked-OR update and preserve completely zero bubbles.
Retain payload's original jump-link choice for valid blocking JALR
launch into pending_payload_q, including alignment/trap and prediction
metadata. Keep existing fast arithmetic and link forwarding sources
separate. Do not add one-hot ALU opcode flops or change ADD/SUB,
barrel shifters, comparators or M arithmetic. This final refinement is
not present in the measured 97.913 MHz prototype and has not been timed.

Use instruction ownership rather than transfer events in the operand
DATA selection masks. Fast ownership requires valid nonblocking EX
work and no pending instruction. Link ownership additionally chooses
the direct-jump link. Completed-source ownership is pending_q with
its captured, trap-qualified payload. MEM ownership is its current
valid, trap-qualified EX/MEM producer. Remove fast_emit/link_emit/
completed_emit and wb_accept from forwarding data masks while
retaining operation-kind, reg_write, nonload, source provenance, x0,
target alignment and final trap qualification. Owner kinds remain
mutually exclusive. Keep independent older matches and youngest
qualified-writer priority so a suppressed trapping writer exposes
the correct older source. Loads never forward effective addresses.

Keep all transfer events unchanged for unit request/consume, EX/MEM
movement, MEM acceptance, predictor training, retirement and physical
register writes. The same hazard hold/flush controls continue to
govern complete operand capture. During an older dmem wait or an
unfinished M result data candidates may be transient, but capture
is inhibited. A pending result is accepted only when execute_busy
releases it; reset and accepted recovery clear the operand bank.
Prove equivalence at the acceptance boundary, not for unobserved
combinational data during a hold. Never accept an unavailable youngest
load or M result by falling back to an older RF or MEM value.

For replacing decoded provenance, compare incoming sources directly
against the current decoded writer that will enter EX, before the
late hold-dependent next-tag mux. Compare concrete fast and pending
MEM destinations independently with the incoming source. Capture
these matches only through the existing decoded acceptance. When
replacement is possible MEM is not held and pending work is complete;
a held MEM candidate cannot coincide with new decode capture. Preserve
all original provenance rebasing during actual holds. Keep effective
next-tag diagnostics used by tests without putting their late mux
back into the matching data path. Retain final result/trap qualification
after matching exactly as the original forwarding policy requires.

Preserve every top-level port, full PC/address, default-illegal and
SYSTEM policy, alignment trap, real and ALTOPS M result, exact RVFI
operands/successors/memory fields, contiguous retirement order and
exactly-once memory effects. Extend directed tests for idle/invalid
EX records, launch bubbles, held requests, stale pending ownership,
same-rd producer ages, trap-suppressed fallback, WB draining during
holds, dependent loads, blocking completion, reset and recovery.
Existing zero-bubble and immutable-operand assertions remain intact.
Compare accepted operand values with independent architectural
results; preserve all existing unit, formal, stalled ISS and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker gates.

Estimate six percent higher fitness with unchanged cycles and low
confidence pending complete candidate vendor timing. The measured 2.03 percent prototype gain is below acceptance; the
six percent estimate is for the final emission/link fusion, not that
measured prototype. No accepted improvement has been established. At unchanged
cycles acceptance requires median Fmax above 100.375206 MHz and
fitness above 233.61364. Removing redundant control masks can shorten
both fast-result capture and operand delivery without extra flops;
the competing ALU/load-return paths and vendor mapping may cap gain.
Judge all three placement options and actual bracketed throughput.

title: Give execution result lanes stable ownership and transfer-independent provenance
motivation:
The champion scores 223.34 at median Gowin Fmax 95.961 MHz and
4,296,564 bracketed CoreMark cycles. It already separates fetch,
decoded metadata and complete execution operands, but its producer
matching and operand muxes still predict physical movement using
late dmemReady, flush, hold and completion-consume controls. Recent
r13s2/r14s2 results expose readiness-to-provenance/operand paths.
r13s1 combined persistent routing with RF snapshots and an LSU lane,
losing 8.77 percent with a competing branch-successor path. This
proposal isolates the operand stage's ownership and capture boundary.
Local probes reject result banking alone (96.586 MHz, unchanged
cycles), registered-only forwarding (92.076 MHz, 4,554,429 cycles),
banking with ownership-only data masks (86.746 MHz, unchanged cycles),
and banked raw load returns (96.481 MHz, 4,508,917 cycles). These
results identify the omitted late provenance controls as a necessary
target and argue against introducing additional dependency bubbles.
The isolated ownership-and-provenance probe reaches 94.905 MHz,
with its worst path still running through the generic ALU/result path
into data memory. The final proposal therefore applies stable ownership
across a banked execution boundary as one producer-lane topology; it is
not the isolated control probe. This complete combination has not yet
been timed and no accepted improvement is claimed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the existing decoded/operand-read stage a transfer-independent
producer-ownership interface. Register source matches against stable
instruction owners, and select continuously available producer words
by those matches and architectural eligibility. Keep actual readiness,
redirects, launch/consume and emission on instruction movement and
operand-bank capture. This is one operand-stage topology change with
unchanged pipeline depth, instruction latency, register-file storage,
execution arithmetic and predictor policy. Each concrete result lane
retains its own registered data and uses the shared in-order owner for
selection and side effects.

Exploit the existing decoded capture invariant: a fetch head replaces
decoded_q only when stall_id is false and neither reset nor accepted
recovery applies. On every such capture edge, hold_ex and the load-use
flush are false, so the next EX owner is the current decoded record.
Form next_ex_tag directly from decoded_q's destination, valid and
possible-writer intent. Remove its hold_ex/flush/reset destination and
writer muxes. Values on noncapture edges are irrelevant and must never
be sampled. Preserve possible load writers and nonzero-source matching.

Likewise match the incoming fetch-head sources to independently
observable EX owners before the late fast_emit/completed_emit/held_emit
controls. The possible next MEM writer is either a valid nonblocking
current EX instruction, including loads, or the valid captured pending
completion owner. A genuine older MEM hold prevents decoded capture,
so an additional held-EX/MEM destination arm is unnecessary for these
incoming matches. Pending validity and operation classification must
distinguish the two owners; a stale pending payload cannot match after
consume or cancellation. Completion may be matched before done, since
execute_busy prevents capture until it can actually transfer. Do not
use a post-handshake destination mux for either source comparison.

Select EX fast arithmetic, direct-jump link and pending completion
values by registered source provenance, their stable owning instruction,
nonzero destination and final trap qualification. Fast and link owners
exclude all blocking MUL/DIV/JALR instructions and a pending completion;
completion ownership requires pending_valid and its original captured
write intent. Remove dmemReady, fast_emit, link_emit, pending_consume
and wb_accept from the wide data-source masks. The MEM candidate may
expose its final qualified load/ALU value continuously while its record
owns that position: a genuine memory wait prevents operand capture.
Retain independent older matches and youngest qualified writer priority,
so a trapping younger writer exposes the correct older value. A load
in EX remains unavailable and never forwards its effective address.

Keep actual transfer signals for physical stage updates, incoming
instruction acceptance, unit request/consume, memory side effects,
training and retirement. Preserve the existing provenance rebasing
while decoded_q is held, based on actual movement of older records;
departed writers remain recoverable through the write-first RF.
Keep complete raw and ALU operand flops immutable during holds, with
reset/recovery dominant. No unavailable load or pending result can be
accepted merely because a data candidate is visible. Capture must
remain blocked until the youngest required value is ready. Add checks
that decoded acceptance implies the assumptions used to simplify tag
prediction and that every accepted nonzero operand equals the youngest
preceding qualified writer's exact value.

This removes handshake-dependent destination prediction as well as
handshake-dependent word selection, addressing the path left behind
by the ownership-only probe. At the existing EX/MEM edge, give scalar ALU data, direct-jump link,
blocking completion and LSU requests their own data registers. A shared
registered class/metadata owner identifies the active lane. Register the
LSU address directly from a native dedicated ADD of complete operands;
keep generic ALU, jump-link and completion selections out of its input.
Capture replicated store data, mask and alignment-qualified enables
beside it. Bank writes use actual advance and local enables; a genuine
MEM hold preserves the complete active packet. Drive the timed dmem
outputs from the owned request bank. Unowned data can retain their old
values but never create a request or forwarding owner. Select accepted
nonload WB data from registered banks after this boundary, retaining
exact load extraction and current accepted-load latency.

To avoid the 37-cell branch-successor path exposed by r13s1, capture
branch outcome, target legality and recovery as narrow decisions
separately from the target and PC+4 words at that same edge. Select the
successor from these registered decisions in MEM; accepted-MEM redirect
and training timing remain unchanged. Preserve the resolving instruction
on recovery, kill younger lane owners, and qualify pending completion by
its valid captured owner. Do not retain generic payload masks or packet
merges ahead of lane data flops. This is a single stable-owner execution
pipeline topology: early matching, continuously owned bypass sources and
independent registered results share one in-order instruction identity.
Do not add raw-return stages, RF snapshots, synchronous RF RAMs,
arithmetic before complete operands or extra result-dependency bubbles.
Preserve nret=1 and all top-level ports, full PCs and addresses,
default-illegal and SYSTEM decoding, alignment traps, real and ALTOPS
RV32M results, exact RVFI operands/successors, contiguous order and
exactly-once memory effects. Require existing unit tests, unchanged
formal, stalled ISS cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker
validation. Score median vendor Fmax times measured bracketed cycles.
At unchanged cycles, acceptance needs Fmax above 100.375206 MHz and
fitness above 233.61364. Project a six percent gain with low confidence;
capture-enable/provenance-rebase fanout, RF reads, post-register result selection and scalar arithmetic can
limit it. Component results are not evidence
that the final ownership-and-provenance change crosses acceptance.

title: Predictor-guided eight-word target-path replay hides fetch stalls
motivation:
The champion already predicts common transfers, but every correctly
predicted target and following instruction still waits for the roughly
22 percent instruction-bus stalls. Recent larger target tables and
instruction-derived target predictors saved only about three percent
of CoreMark cycles and reduced median Gowin frequency. A small learned
target-path payload can make an existing correct prediction useful
during bus stalls without increasing the branch target lookup width.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion already predicts common transfers, but every correctly

22 percent instruction-bus stalls. Recent larger target tables and
instruction-derived target predictors saved only about three percent

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend the existing 32-entry fully tagged BTB with an eight-instruction
target-path replay buffer. Keep its current target, direction counters,
accepted-MEM training, indexed lookup, precise successor recovery and
all three fixed registered fetch records. The single architectural
change is that a committed target prediction can also supply previously
observed instruction words from that target's straight-line path.

Each BTB row owns eight instruction words for target+0,+4,...,+28 and
eight independently valid payload bits. Learn words only from accepted
instruction-bus responses at those full aligned addresses, never from
replayed words or an unaccepted bus word. Enter a replay context only
when an accepted fetch selects that row's target prediction; snapshot
the full base target and row identity. A matching valid payload supplies
its word to the existing fetched-record input and can enqueue even
when imem_ready is low. A payload miss uses the ordinary bus handshake.
Every supplied word still gets the ordinary BTB prediction at its own
full PC, and that prediction is snapshotted with the word. Sequential
movement consumes the next offset; another selected target establishes
a new context, while leaving the eight-word interval ends replay. Do not
bypass the fixed head registers or change decode and operand capture.

Associate every replay context with its owner's full target. Replacement,
invalidation, or a changed full target cancels
old payload validity and an active context for that row. A same-target
counter update retains payload. Reset clears validity and context and
cancels pending fills. Accepted architectural recovery flushes queue
and context and keeps its existing full resolved target authority.
FENCE.I acceptance invalidates all instruction payloads and squashes
younger prefetched words before resuming at its resolved successor,
preserving instruction-stream synchronization. Never suppress genuine
bus writes, memory waits, traps, retirement, or architectural recovery.

Keep payload storage and read separate from the existing indexed BTB
target lookup. Use a registered five-bit replay row and three-bit offset
and eight constant-offset banks of 32 separate word-register leaves with
balanced masked-OR reads and local validity bits, following the successful
register-file storage style. Do not concatenate payloads to target RAM or
introduce a live instruction bypass into decode. At a bus-ready enqueue,
prefer the live bus word; use replay only to hide an actual bus stall.
An accepted enqueue advances PC exactly once from either source; full-queue
backpressure still holds PC and context unchanged. Offset seven terminates
sequential replay unless another selected prediction starts a new context.
Keep full target+4*offset address semantics, including 32-bit wraparound.

Register a fill event containing row, offset and accepted bus word, and
apply it one edge later. Separately register a row-invalidation event at
the existing BTB commit edge when validity, full source tag or full target
association changes. Add an old-target snapshot to training ingress and
forward the older complete post-update target on consecutive same-row
events, alongside the existing tag/counter snapshots. Compare registered
old/post values; do not feed live indexed table reads directly into
payload write controls. Decode registered fill/invalidation indices at
constant leaves. Invalidation takes priority over a same-row fill, rejecting
bus data captured under old ownership on the replacement edge. An unchanged
tag/target counter update retains payloads. Clear an active context immediately
when its owner changes, and suppress a new context whose row changes on the
current commit or awaits pending invalidation. This prevents a new target
association from consuming old valid bits while delayed invalidation drains.
Recovery cancels younger fills and context while preserving accepted BTB
training and required invalidation. Reset and FENCE.I cancel pending fills
and all payload validity. Payload words need no reset if separate word leaves
remain flops and uninitialized words are masked by resettable validity.
Inspect synthesis for absorbed RAM registers and measure the routing cost.

Export synchronization only for an accepted legal FENCE.I record, recognized
by opcode 0x0f and funct3=1 under the unchanged decoder policy. Include this
event in the existing accepted-MEM redirect to its resolved PC+4, invalidating
payloads and younger queue/decode/EX work while the FENCE.I itself retires
exactly once. Preserve ordinary FENCE and all decoder legality assertions.
Reuse is restricted to a selected prediction's eight-word sequential path;
do not add a general instruction-cache lookup or change direction accuracy.

Preserve nret=1 and all external ports, full PCs and targets, validated
default-illegal decoding, resolved RVFI operands and successors,
contiguous retirement order, RV32M/ALTOPS behavior and exactly-once
memory effects. Run unchanged formal, unit, stalled ISS cosim and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/OOB gates. Measure actual bracketed
cycles times median vendor Fmax; acceptance requires more than 233.61
iterations/second. The proposed six percent gain is an estimate:
insufficient target-path reuse or payload routing may erase it.

Exploratory evidence: fresh baseline simulation reproduces 4,296,564
bracketed cycles. Four-word replay measures 4,113,486; eight-word replay
measures 4,057,613, a 5.889 percent throughput gain at unchanged Fmax.
The eight-word prototype with registered fills and invalidations reproduces
exactly 4,057,613 cycles. All runs finish with canonical CRCs, success UART,
valid timing markers and no OOB. A reference replay also reproduces all
73,619 champion prediction misses. Initial indexed four-word storage with
direct invalidation controls measures only 75.938 MHz on Gowin placement
option 1, exposing a tag-RAM-to-payload-validity path; its storage/control
shape is explicitly excluded above. The final organization needs independent
median timing. At 4,057,613 cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above
94.791375 MHz. These temporary probes establish sizing and cycle behavior,
not full formal validation or measured fitness for the final implementation
including FENCE.I synchronization. Added selection, area and routing remain
material risks, so confidence is low.
